title.zh: 卷一百五十二 列傳第七十七 張姜武李宋
title.en: Volume 152 Biographies 77: Zhang, Jiang, Wu, Li, Song
title.raw: 卷一百五十二 列傳第七十七 張姜武李宋 Volume 152 Biographies 77: Zhang, Jiang, Wu, Li, Song

sentences.zh: 張姜武李宋

translations.literal: Zhang, Jiang, Wu, Li, Song
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, Jiang, Wu, Li, and Song

sentences.zh: 張鎰，字季權，一字公度，國子祭酒後胤五世孫也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi, style name Jiquan, also styled Gongdu, was a descendant five generations removed from the heir of the Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi, courtesy name Jiquan and also known as Gongdu, was five generations removed from the heir of a Director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 父齊丘，朔方節度使、東都留守。

translations.literal: His father Qiqiu was military commissioner of Shuofang and left-behind commissioner of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qiqiu served as military commissioner of Shuofang and as left-behind commissioner of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 鎰以蔭授左衛兵曹參軍，郭子儀表為元帥府判官，遷累殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Yi received appointment as Left Guard Army staff officer by hereditary privilege; Guo Ziyi recommended him as judge of the marshal's headquarters, and he was promoted in succession to Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Yi entered service as a Left Guard Army staff officer through hereditary privilege. Guo Ziyi recommended him as judge of the marshal's headquarters, and he rose in due course to the post of Palace Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 乾元初，華原令盧樅以公事譙責邑人齊令詵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qianyuan era, Hua Yuan magistrate Lu Cong rebuked a townsman, Qi Lingshen, on official business.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianyuan era, Lu Cong, magistrate of Hua Yuan, publicly rebuked a local man named Qi Lingshen in the course of official business.

sentences.zh: 令詵，宦人也，銜之，構樅罪。

translations.literal: Lingshen was a eunuch; he harbored resentment and fabricated a charge against Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Lingshen was a eunuch. He bore a grudge and contrived to have Cong charged with a crime.

sentences.zh: 鎰按驗當免官，有司承風以死論。

translations.literal: Yi investigated and verified that Cong should be dismissed from office, but the authorities, following the prevailing wind, argued for the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Yi investigated the case and found that Cong deserved dismissal from office, but the authorities, swayed by the prevailing mood, pressed for a death sentence.

sentences.zh: 鎰不直之，乃白其母曰：「今理樅，樅免死而鎰坐貶。

translations.literal: Yi did not consider this right and told his mother, saying: "If I now try Cong's case, Cong will escape death while Yi will suffer demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Yi would not endorse this course. He told his mother, "If I now see justice done for Cong, he will escape death, but I will be demoted.

sentences.zh: 嘿則負官，貶則為太夫人憂，敢問所安？」

translations.literal: If I keep silent I fail in my office; if I am demoted I cause worry to the Grand Lady—dare I ask where my peace lies?"
translations.idiomatic: If I stay silent, I fail my office; if I am demoted, I bring distress upon you, my lady. Where, then, should I find my peace?"

sentences.zh: 母曰：「兒無累於道，吾所安也。」

translations.literal: His mother said: "My son, you are not burdening the Way—that is my peace."
translations.idiomatic: His mother replied, "My son, so long as you do not compromise the Way, that is peace enough for me."

sentences.zh: 遂執正其罪，樅得流，鎰貶撫州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: He then upheld the proper penalty: Cong was banished, and Yi was demoted to Registrar of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He upheld the proper sentence. Cong was banished, and Yi was demoted to registrar of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 徙晉陵令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be magistrate of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to serve as magistrate of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 江西觀察使張鎬表為判官，遷屯田、右司二員外郎。

translations.literal: Jiangxi observation commissioner Zhang Gao recommended him as judge; he was promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of State Farms and Vice Director of the Right Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gao, observation commissioner of Jiangxi, recommended him as a judge. He was promoted to vice director of the Bureau of State Farms and vice director of the Right Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 居母喪，以孝聞。

translations.literal: While mourning his mother he became known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: During his mother's mourning period he became renowned for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 不妄交遊，特與楊綰、崔祐甫善。

translations.literal: He did not make friends lightly and was especially close to Yang Guan and Cui Youfu.
translations.idiomatic: He did not cultivate friendships lightly and was especially close to Yang Guan and Cui Youfu.

sentences.zh: 大歷初，出為濠州刺史，政條清簡，延經術士講教生徒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dali era he went out as prefect of Hao; his administrative measures were clear and simple, and he invited scholars of the classics to lecture and teach students.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dali era he was appointed prefect of Hao. His administration was clear and restrained, and he invited classical scholars to lecture and instruct students.

sentences.zh: 比去，州升明經者四十人。

translations.literal: By the time he left, forty men of the prefecture had passed the Mingjing examination.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he left office, forty men from the prefecture had passed the Mingjing examination.

sentences.zh: 李靈耀反於汴，鎰團閱鄉兵嚴守禦，有詔褒美，擢侍御史，兼緣淮鎮守使。

translations.literal: When Li Lingyao rebelled at Bian, Yi mustered and reviewed local militia to defend strictly; an edict praised him, and he was promoted to Attending Censor, concurrently serving as commissioner for defense along the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Lingyao rebelled at Bian, Yi mustered the local militia and organized a tight defense. The court issued an edict praising him, promoted him to Attending Censor, and appointed him concurrently as commissioner for defense along the Huai.

sentences.zh: 以最遷壽州刺史。

translations.literal: For outstanding merit he was transferred to be prefect of Shou.
translations.idiomatic: On account of outstanding merit he was transferred to serve as prefect of Shou.

sentences.zh: 歷江西、河中觀察使。

translations.literal: He successively served as observation commissioner of Jiangxi and Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as observation commissioner of Jiangxi and of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 不閱旬，改汴滑節度使，以病固辭，詔留私第。

translations.literal: Within less than ten days he was changed to military commissioner of Biansui; he firmly declined on grounds of illness, and an edict ordered him to remain at his private residence.
translations.idiomatic: Within less than ten days he was reassigned as military commissioner of Biansui. He firmly declined on grounds of illness, and the emperor ordered him to remain at his private residence.

sentences.zh: 建中二年，拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianzhong he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianzhong he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrent Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 明年，以兩河用兵，詔省薄禦膳及皇太子食物，鎰因奏減堂餐錢及百官稟奉三分一，以助用度。

translations.literal: The next year, because troops were deployed in the two He regions, an edict ordered economies in the imperial table and the crown prince's provisions; Yi thereupon memorialized to reduce hall-meal funds and the salaries of all officials by one third to assist expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, with armies engaged in the two He regions, the court ordered reductions in the imperial table and the crown prince's provisions. Yi memorialized to cut hall-meal allowances and official salaries by one third to help meet wartime expenses.

sentences.zh: 時黜陟使裴伯言薦潞州處士田佐時，詔除右拾遺、集賢院直學士。

translations.literal: At that time the promotion-and-demotion commissioner Pei Boyan recommended the Lu prefecture recluse Tian Zuoshi; an edict appointed him Right Reminder and direct academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Pei Boyan, commissioner for promotions and demotions, recommended Tian Zuoshi, a recluse of Lu prefecture. An edict appointed him Right Reminder and direct academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 鎰以為禮輕，恐士不勸，復詔州縣吏以絹百匹、粟百石就家致聘，佐時卒不至。

translations.literal: Yi considered the ceremonial treatment too light and feared scholars would not be encouraged; another edict ordered prefectural and county officials to go to his home with one hundred bolts of silk and one hundred shi of grain to extend the invitation, but Zuoshi in the end did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Yi judged the ceremonial treatment too slight and feared it would not encourage scholars. The court then ordered local officials to visit his home with one hundred bolts of silk and one hundred shi of grain, but Zuoshi never came.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀婿太仆卿趙縱為奴告，下御史劾治，而奴留內侍省。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi's son-in-law, Minister of the Stud Zhao Zong, was denounced by a slave; the case was sent down to the censorate for investigation, but the slave was kept in the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zong, Minister of the Stud and son-in-law of Guo Ziyi, was denounced by a slave. The case was referred to the censorate for investigation, yet the slave was kept in the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 鎰奏言：「貞觀時有奴告其主謀反者，太宗曰：『謀反理不獨成，尚當有他人論之，豈藉奴告耶？』

translations.literal: Yi memorialized, saying: "In the Zhenguan era, when a slave reported that his master plotted rebellion, Taizong said: 'The charge of rebellion cannot stand on its own; others should still debate it—how can one rely on a slave's report?
translations.idiomatic: Yi memorialized: "In the Zhenguan era, when a slave accused his master of plotting rebellion, Emperor Taizong said, 'A charge of rebellion cannot stand on its own. Others must still weigh the case—how can one rely on a slave's accusation?

sentences.zh: 乃著令：奴告主者斬。

translations.literal: He then established a statute: slaves who reported their masters were to be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He then promulgated a statute: any slave who denounced his master was to be executed.

sentences.zh: 由是賤不得幹貴，下不得淩上，教本既修，悖亂不萌。

translations.literal: Thus the base could not interfere with the noble, nor the low overbear upon the high; fundamental instruction was already cultivated, and perverse disorder did not sprout.
translations.idiomatic: From that time the low could not meddle with the high, nor inferiors overbear their superiors. Once the roots of instruction were secured, perverse disorder did not arise.

sentences.zh: 頃者，長安令李濟以奴得罪，萬年令霍晏因婢坐譴。

translations.literal: Recently, Chang'an magistrate Li Ji was punished because of a slave, and Wannian magistrate Huo Yan was reprimanded on account of a maid.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Chang'an magistrate Li Ji was punished on account of a slave, and Wannian magistrate Huo Yan was censured because of a maid.

sentences.zh: 輿臺下類，主反畏之，悖慢成風，漸不可長。

translations.literal: Carriage attendants and menials—masters instead feared them; perversity and insolence became a fashion, and the trend could not be allowed to grow.
translations.idiomatic: Menials and carriage attendants had come to be feared by their masters. Insolence had become a fashion, and the trend could not be allowed to spread.

sentences.zh: 建中元年五月辛卯詔書：奴婢告主，非謀叛者，同自首法，並準律論。

translations.literal: The edict of the first year of Jianzhong, fifth month, day xinmao: when slaves or maids reported their masters, if it was not plotting rebellion, it was treated like the law on voluntary surrender, and both were judged according to statute.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of the fifth month of the first year of Jianzhong, on the day xinmao, ruled that when slaves or maids denounced their masters in cases other than rebellion, the matter was handled under the law on voluntary surrender and both parties were judged by statute.

sentences.zh: 由是獄訴衰息。

translations.literal: Because of this, prison suits declined and ceased.
translations.idiomatic: After that, such lawsuits declined sharply.

sentences.zh: 今縱事非叛逆，而奴留禁中，獨下縱獄，情所不厭。

translations.literal: Now Zong's affair is not rebellion, yet the slave is kept in the inner palace while only Zong is sent down to prison—this is what feeling cannot accept.
translations.idiomatic: Zong's case is not one of rebellion, yet the slave is kept in the inner palace while only Zong is sent to prison. Such a course is intolerable to right feeling.

sentences.zh: 且將帥功孰大於子儀，冢土僅乾，兩婿前已得罪，縱復繼之，不數月斥其三婿。

translations.literal: Moreover, among generals whose merit was greater than Ziyi's? His ancestral tomb had scarcely dried when two sons-in-law had already been punished; if Zong were punished in turn, within a few months all three sons-in-law would be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, what general's merit exceeded Guo Ziyi's? His ancestral tomb had scarcely dried when two sons-in-law had already been punished. If Zong were punished as well, within a few months all three sons-in-law would have been cast aside.

sentences.zh: 假令縱實犯法，事不緣奴，尚宜錄勛念亡，以從蕩宥，況為奴所訴耶？

translations.literal: Even supposing Zong truly violated the law and the matter did not arise from the slave, it would still be fitting to record his merit and remember the dead, granting broad pardon—how much more when he is denounced by a slave?
translations.idiomatic: Even if Zong had truly broken the law and the matter had nothing to do with the slave, the court should still have weighed his merit and remembered the dead man, granting broad pardon. How much less should this be done when the charge comes from a slave?

sentences.zh: 陛下方貴武臣以討賊，彼雖見寵一時，不能忘懷於異日也。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty is just now honoring military ministers to suppress rebels; though they may be favored for a time, they cannot put the matter from their hearts on another day."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is now honoring military men to suppress rebels. Though they may enjoy favor for the moment, they will not forget such treatment when another day comes."

sentences.zh: 帝納之，貶縱循州司馬，杖奴死。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted this, demoted Zong to Sima of Xun prefecture, and had the slave beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice, demoted Zong to defender of Xun prefecture, and had the slave beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 鎰召子儀家僮數百，暴示奴屍。

translations.literal: Yi summoned several hundred of Ziyi's household servants and publicly displayed the slave's corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Yi summoned several hundred of Ziyi's household servants and publicly displayed the slave's corpse.

sentences.zh: 盧杞忌鎰剛直，欲去之。

translations.literal: Lu Qi resented Yi's firm uprightness and wished to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi resented Yi's firm uprightness and sought to remove him.

sentences.zh: 時朱泚以盧龍卒戍鳳翔，帝擇人以代，杞即謬曰：「鳳翔將校，班秩素高，非宰相信臣，不可鎮撫，臣宜行。」

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Ci was garrisoning Fengxiang with Lulong troops; the emperor chose a man to replace him. Qi immediately spoke falsely, saying: "Fengxiang's officers and men have always held high rank and standing; none but a chief minister or trusted minister can pacify and command them—I ought to go."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhu Ci was garrisoning Fengxiang with troops from Lulong, and the emperor sought someone to replace him. Qi at once said deceitfully, "The officers at Fengxiang have always held high rank. None but a chief minister or a trusted minister of the throne can command them. I ought to go."

sentences.zh: 帝不許，杞復曰：「陛下必以臣容貌蕞陋，不為三軍所信，恐後生變，臣不敢自謀，惟陛下擇之。」

translations.literal: The emperor did not consent. Qi again said: "If Your Majesty must think my appearance mean and ugly and that the Three Armies will not trust me, fearing trouble later, I dare not decide for myself—let Your Majesty choose."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused. Qi said again, "If Your Majesty thinks my appearance too mean to inspire the army's trust and fears trouble later, I dare not decide for myself. Let Your Majesty choose."

sentences.zh: 帝乃顧鎰曰：「文武兼資，望重內外，無易卿者，其為朕撫盧龍士。」

translations.literal: The emperor then turned to Yi and said: "You combine civil and military ability and are weighty within and without; there is no one to replace you—go and pacify the Lulong troops for Us."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then turned to Yi and said, "You combine civil and military talent and command respect within and without the court. There is no one to replace you. Go and pacify the Lulong troops for me."

sentences.zh: 乃以中書侍郎為鳳翔、隴右節度使。

translations.literal: He was then made Vice Director of the Secretariat and military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou.

sentences.zh: 鎰知為杞陰中，然辭窮，因再拜受詔。

translations.literal: Yi knew he had been struck down in secret by Qi, but his words were exhausted; he therefore bowed twice and accepted the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Yi knew Qi had maneuvered against him in secret, but he had no reply left. He bowed twice and accepted the edict.

sentences.zh: 頃之，與吐蕃相尚結贊盟清水，約牛馬為牲。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, with the Tibetan minister Shang Jiezan he made alliance at Qingshui, agreeing to use cattle and horses as sacrificial victims.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he made alliance with the Tibetan minister Shang Jiezan at Qingshui, agreeing to offer cattle and horses as sacrificial victims.

sentences.zh: 鎰恥與盟，將末殺其禮，乃紿語吐蕃，以羊豕犬代之。

translations.literal: Yi was ashamed to join in the alliance and, about to belittle and diminish its ritual, deceived the Tibetans by substituting sheep, pigs, and dogs.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed to join the alliance on equal terms, Yi sought to diminish its ritual standing. He deceived the Tibetans by substituting sheep, pigs, and dogs for the agreed victims.

sentences.zh: 帝幸奉天，鎰罄家貲將自獻行在。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Fengtian, Yi exhausted his family wealth to offer it personally to the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Fengtian, Yi exhausted his family wealth to send it to the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 而營將李楚琳者，嘗事朱泚，得其心。

translations.literal: But the camp general Li Chulin had once served Zhu Ci and won his heart.
translations.idiomatic: But a camp general named Li Chulin had once served Zhu Ci and won his confidence.

sentences.zh: 軍司馬齊映等謀曰：「楚琳必為亂。」

translations.literal: Army Vice Marshal Qi Ying and others plotted, saying: "Chulin is certain to make trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Army Vice Marshal Qi Ying and others plotted together, saying, "Chulin is certain to rebel."

sentences.zh: 乃遣屯隴州。

translations.literal: They then dispatched him to garrison Long prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: They then ordered him transferred to garrison Long prefecture.

sentences.zh: 楚琳知之，稽故未行。

translations.literal: Chulin learned of this and, citing old grounds, did not depart.
translations.idiomatic: Chulin learned of the plan and, citing old grounds, refused to depart.

sentences.zh: 鎰以帝在外，心憂惑，謂已亟去，不為備。

translations.literal: Yi, because the emperor was abroad, was anxious and unsettled in mind, thinking Chulin would soon leave, and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: With the emperor away from the capital, Yi was anxious and distracted. He assumed Chulin would soon depart and made no preparations.

sentences.zh: 楚琳夜率其黨王汾、李卓、牛僧伽等作亂，齊映自竇出，齊抗托傭，皆免。

translations.literal: Chulin by night led his faction—Wang Fen, Li Zhuo, Niu Sengqie, and others—to make rebellion. Qi Ying escaped through a hole; Qi Kang passed himself off as a hired laborer; both were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Chulin led his followers Wang Fen, Li Zhuo, Niu Sengqie, and others in a night revolt. Qi Ying escaped through a hole in the wall; Qi Kang passed himself off as a hired laborer. Both survived.

sentences.zh: 鎰縋城走，不及遠，與二子為候騎所執，楚琳殺之，屬官王沼、張元度、柳遇、李漵皆死。

translations.literal: Yi let himself down from the wall and fled, but before he had gone far he and his two sons were seized by scout horsemen; Chulin killed them. Subordinate officials Wang Zhao, Zhang Yuandu, Liu Yu, and Li Qin all died.
translations.idiomatic: Yi lowered himself from the city wall and fled, but before he had gone far he and his two sons were seized by scout horsemen and killed by Chulin. Subordinate officials Wang Zhao, Zhang Yuandu, Liu Yu, and Li Qin also died.

sentences.zh: 詔贈鎰太子太傅。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously enfeoffed Yi as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously enfeoffed Yi as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 姜公輔，愛州日南人。

translations.literal: Jiang Gongfu was a man of Rinan in Ai prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Gongfu was a native of Rinan in Ai prefecture.

sentences.zh: 第進士，補校書郎，以制策異等授右拾遺，為翰林學士。

translations.literal: He placed in the jinshi examination, was appointed collator, and for distinguished performance in the policy examination was made Right Reminder and Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed collator. For distinguished performance in the policy examination he was made Right Reminder and Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 歲滿當遷，上書以母老賴祿而養，求兼京兆戶曹參軍事。

translations.literal: When his term was complete and he was due for promotion, he memorialized that his mother was old and depended on his salary for support, and requested concurrently to serve as registrar of the Jingzhao household bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended and promotion was due, he memorialized that his aged mother depended on his salary and asked to serve concurrently as registrar of the Jingzhao household bureau.

sentences.zh: 公輔有高材，每進見，敷奏詳亮，德宗器之。

translations.literal: Gongfu had great talent; whenever he entered audience his presentations were detailed and clear, and Dezong valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Gongfu possessed great talent. Whenever he appeared before the throne his presentations were thorough and lucid, and Emperor Dezong valued him highly.

sentences.zh: 朱滔助田悅也，以蜜裹書間道邀泚，太原馬燧獲之，泚不知也，召還京師。

translations.literal: When Zhu Tao was aiding Tian Yue, he sent a letter wrapped in honey by a secret route to invite Ci; Ma Sui of Taiyuan seized it. Ci did not know of this and was summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhu Tao was aiding Tian Yue, he sent a letter wrapped in honey by a secret route inviting Zhu Ci to join him. Ma Sui of Taiyuan intercepted it. Ci knew nothing of this and was summoned back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 公輔諫曰：「陛下若不能坦懷待泚，不如誅之，養虎無自詒害。」

translations.literal: Gongfu remonstrated, saying: "If Your Majesty cannot treat Ci with open sincerity, it would be better to execute him—do not rear a tiger and bring harm upon yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Gongfu remonstrated: "If Your Majesty cannot receive Ci with open sincerity, it would be better to execute him. Do not rear a tiger and bring harm upon yourself."

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 俄而涇師亂，帝自苑門出，公輔叩馬諫曰：「泚嘗帥涇原，得士心，向以滔叛奪之兵，居常怫郁不自聊，請馳騎捕取以從，無為群兇得之。」

translations.literal: Shortly the Jing army rebelled; the emperor went out through the park gate. Gongfu seized the horse's bridle and remonstrated: "Ci once commanded Jingyuan and won the soldiers' hearts. Because Tao rebelled his troops were taken away; he has constantly been resentful and ill at ease. I beg to ride swiftly and seize him to follow Your Majesty—do not let the mass of villains get him."
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Jing army rebelled, and the emperor fled through the park gate. Gongfu seized the bridle and remonstrated: "Ci once commanded Jingyuan and won the soldiers' loyalty. When Tao rebelled, his troops were taken from him, and he has brooded ever since. Let me ride ahead and seize him to follow Your Majesty—do not let the rebels get to him first."

sentences.zh: 帝倉卒不及聽。

translations.literal: In his haste the emperor had no time to listen.
translations.idiomatic: In his haste the emperor had no time to listen.

sentences.zh: 既行，欲駐鳳翔倚張鎰。

translations.literal: After setting out, he wished to halt at Fengxiang and rely on Zhang Yi.
translations.idiomatic: After setting out, he wished to halt at Fengxiang and rely on Zhang Yi.

sentences.zh: 公輔曰：「鎰雖信臣，然文吏也，所領皆朱泚部曲，漁陽突騎，泚若立，涇軍且有變，非萬全策也。」

translations.literal: Gongfu said: "Though Yi is a trusted minister, he is a civil official; those he commands are all Zhu Ci's former troops—Fanyang shock cavalry. If Ci were installed, the Jing army would also change—this is not a plan of complete safety."
translations.idiomatic: Gongfu said, "Yi is a trusted minister, but he is a civil official. The troops under his command are Zhu Ci's old followers—Fanyang shock cavalry. If Ci were installed in power, the Jing army would turn as well. This is not a plan of complete safety."

sentences.zh: 帝亦記桑道茂言，遂之奉天。

translations.literal: The emperor also remembered Sang Daomao's words and therefore went on to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also recalled the prophecy of Sang Daomao and continued on to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 不數日，鳳翔果亂，殺鎰。

translations.literal: Within a few days Fengxiang did indeed fall into disorder, and Yi was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days Fengxiang did indeed erupt in disorder, and Yi was killed.

sentences.zh: 帝在奉天，有言泚反者，請為守備。

translations.literal: While the emperor was at Fengtian, someone said Ci had rebelled and asked that defenses be made.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was at Fengtian, someone reported that Ci had rebelled and urged defensive preparations.

sentences.zh: 盧杞曰：「泚忠正篤實，奈何言其叛，傷大臣心！

translations.literal: Lu Qi said: "Ci is loyal, upright, and sincere—how can you speak of his rebellion and wound a great minister's heart!
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi said, "Ci is loyal, upright, and sincere—how can you speak of rebellion and wound a great minister's heart!

sentences.zh: 請百口保之。」

translations.literal: I beg to guarantee him with a hundred mouths."
translations.idiomatic: I stake a hundred lives on his loyalty."

sentences.zh: 帝知群臣多勸杞奉迎乘輿者，乃詔諸道兵距城一舍止。

translations.literal: The emperor knew that many ministers were urging Qi to welcome back the imperial carriage, and therefore issued an edict that armies of the various circuits halt one stage from the city.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew that many ministers were urging Qi to welcome the imperial carriage back to the capital. He therefore ordered the armies of the various circuits to halt one stage from the city.

sentences.zh: 公輔曰：「王者不嚴羽衛，無以重威靈。

translations.literal: Gongfu said: "A king who does not maintain strict guard and escort cannot give weight to his majesty and numinous authority.
translations.idiomatic: Gongfu said, "A ruler who does not maintain strict guard cannot lend weight to his majesty.

sentences.zh: 今禁旅單寡而士馬處外，為陛下危之。」

translations.literal: Now the palace guard is thin and few while soldiers and horses are stationed outside—I fear this for Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: The palace guard is now thin, while troops and horses remain outside. I fear for Your Majesty's safety."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 悉內諸軍。

translations.literal: He brought all the armies inside.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered all the armies brought within the walls.

sentences.zh: 泚兵果至，如所言，乃擢公輔諫議大夫、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Ci's troops indeed arrived, just as he had said; Gongfu was then promoted to Remonstrating Grand Master and Concurrent Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Ci's troops arrived just as he had predicted. Gongfu was then promoted to Remonstrating Grand Master and concurrent Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 帝徙梁，唐安公主道薨。

translations.literal: When the emperor moved to Liang, Princess Tang'an died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor moved to Liang, Princess Tang'an died on the journey.

sentences.zh: 主性仁孝，許下嫁韋宥，以播遷未克也。

translations.literal: The princess was by nature benevolent and filial; she had been promised in marriage below to Wei You, but because of the wandering exile it had not been accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was by nature benevolent and filial. She had been promised in marriage to Wei You, but the turmoil of exile had prevented the wedding.

sentences.zh: 帝悼之甚，詔厚其葬。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned her deeply and ordered a lavish burial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned her deeply and ordered a lavish burial.

sentences.zh: 公輔諫曰：「即平賊，主必歸葬，今行道宜從儉，以濟軍興。」

translations.literal: Gongfu remonstrated, saying: "Once the rebels are pacified, the princess will certainly be returned for burial; for the present journey one should follow frugality to assist military preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Gongfu remonstrated: "Once the rebels are pacified, the princess will certainly be returned for burial at the capital. For the present journey the funeral should be kept frugal to aid military preparations.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，謂翰林學士陸贄曰：「唐安之葬，不欲事塋壟，令累甓為浮圖，費甚寡約，不容宰相關預，茍欲指朕過爾！」

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and said to Hanlin academician Lu Zhi: "For Tang'an's burial I did not wish to undertake a tomb mound; I ordered stacked bricks made into a pagoda—the expense was very slight and restrained. A chief minister may not interfere; he merely wished to point out my fault!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and said to Hanlin academician Lu Zhi, "For Tang'an's burial I did not wish to raise a tomb mound. I ordered only a brick pagoda, at very modest expense. A chief minister has no business interfering. He merely wished to point out my fault!"

sentences.zh: 贄曰：「公輔官諫議，職宰相，獻替固其分。

translations.literal: Zhi said: "Gongfu holds the office of Remonstrating Grand Master and the duty of chief minister—offering correction is indeed his portion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi replied, "Gongfu holds the office of Remonstrating Grand Master and serves as chief minister. Offering correction is indeed his duty.

sentences.zh: 本立輔臣，朝夕納誨，微而弼之，乃其所也。」

translations.literal: The fundamental purpose in establishing assisting ministers is that morning and evening they present instruction, subtly supporting—this is what is proper to them."
translations.idiomatic: Assisting ministers exist so that morning and evening they may offer instruction and subtly support the throne. That is their proper role."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「不然，朕以公輔才不足以相，而又自求解，朕既許之，內知且罷，故賣直售名爾。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Not so. I considered Gongfu's talent insufficient for the chancellorship, and moreover he himself asked to be released—I already consented. In my heart I knew I would dismiss him, so he is merely selling uprightness to purchase a name."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Not so. I judged Gongfu's talent insufficient for the chancellorship, and he himself asked to be released. I had already agreed in my heart to dismiss him. He is merely selling uprightness to purchase a reputation."

sentences.zh: 遂下遷太子左庶子，以母喪解。

translations.literal: He was therefore demoted to Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent and resigned on account of his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent and resigned when his mother died.

sentences.zh: 復為右庶子。

translations.literal: He was later restored as Right Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He was later restored to the post of Right Mentor.

sentences.zh: 久不遷，陸贄為相，公輔數求官，贄密謂曰：「竇丞相嘗言，為公擬官屢矣，上輒不悅。」

translations.literal: For a long time he was not promoted. When Lu Zhi became chief minister, Gongfu repeatedly sought an office. Zhi secretly told him: "Chief Minister Dou once said that he had repeatedly proposed offices for you, but the emperor was always displeased."
translations.idiomatic: For a long time he received no promotion. When Lu Zhi became chief minister, Gongfu repeatedly sought an appointment. Zhi told him privately, "Chief Minister Dou once said that he had repeatedly proposed offices for you, but the emperor was always displeased."

sentences.zh: 公輔懼，請為道士，未報。

translations.literal: Gongfu was afraid and requested to become a Daoist priest; no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: Gongfu was alarmed and asked to become a Daoist priest. No reply came.

sentences.zh: 它日又言之，帝問故，公輔隱贄言，以參語對。

translations.literal: On another day he spoke of it again; the emperor asked the reason. Gongfu concealed Zhi's words and answered with Dou Can's statement.
translations.idiomatic: On another day he raised the matter again. When the emperor asked why, Gongfu concealed Zhi's words and answered with Dou Can's statement.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，黜公輔泉州別駕，遣使賫詔讓參。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, demoted Gongfu to vice prefect of Quanzhou, and sent an envoy bearing an edict to reprove Can.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged. He demoted Gongfu to vice prefect of Quanzhou and sent an envoy bearing an edict to reprove Dou Can.

sentences.zh: 順宗立，拜吉州刺史，未就官卒。

translations.literal: When Shunzong was enthroned, Gongfu was appointed prefect of Ji, but before taking office he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong was enthroned, Gongfu was appointed prefect of Ji, but he died before taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 憲宗時，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In Xianzong's time he was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xianzong he was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 武元衡，字伯蒼。

translations.literal: Wu Yuanheng, style name Bocang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuanheng, courtesy name Bocang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖載德，則天皇后之族弟。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zaide was a clansman younger brother of Empress Wu Zetian.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zaide was a younger clansman of Empress Wu Zetian.

sentences.zh: 祖平一，有名。

translations.literal: His grandfather Pingyi was famous.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Pingyi was a man of renown.

sentences.zh: 元衡舉進士，累為華原令。

translations.literal: Yuanheng passed the jinshi examination and successively served as magistrate of Huayuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanheng passed the jinshi examination and served in succession as magistrate of Huayuan.

sentences.zh: 畿輔鎮軍督將，皆驕橫橈政，元衡移疾去。

translations.literal: The supervising generals of garrison armies in the capital region were all arrogant and overbearing, thwarting government; Yuanheng pleaded illness and left.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising generals of garrison armies in the capital region were all arrogant and obstructed government. Yuanheng pleaded illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 德宗欽其才，召拜比部員外郎，歲內三遷至右司郎中，以詳整任職。

translations.literal: Dezong admired his talent, summoned and appointed him Vice Director of the Revenue Bureau, and within the year promoted him three times to Director of the Right Secretariat; he discharged his duties with thoroughness and order.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong admired his talent, summoned him, and appointed him Vice Director of the Revenue Bureau. Within a year he was promoted three times to Director of the Right Secretariat, discharging his duties with thoroughness and precision.

sentences.zh: 擢為御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 嘗對延英，帝目送之，曰：「是真宰相器！」

translations.literal: Once, at an audience in Yan Ying Hall, the emperor watched him depart and said: "He is truly material for a chief minister!"
translations.idiomatic: Once, during an audience at Yan Ying Hall, the emperor watched him leave and said, "Here is a man truly fit to be chief minister!"

sentences.zh: 順宗立，王叔文使人誘以為黨，拒不納。

translations.literal: When Shunzong was enthroned, Wang Shuwen sent men to entice him into their faction, but he refused to join.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong took the throne, Wang Shuwen sent men to draw him into their faction, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 俄為山陵儀仗使，監察御史劉禹錫求為判官，元衡不與，叔文滋不悅。

translations.literal: Soon he became Commissioner for Imperial Mausoleum Ceremonies. Palace Attendant Censor Liu Yuxi asked to serve as his judge; Yuanheng would not grant it, and Shuwen grew still more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Commissioner for Imperial Mausoleum Ceremonies. Palace Attendant Censor Liu Yuxi asked to serve as judge on his staff, but Yuanheng refused, and Shuwen grew all the more displeased.

sentences.zh: 數日，改太子右庶子。

translations.literal: Within a few days he was transferred to Right Vice Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days he was reassigned as Right Vice Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 會冊皇太子，元衡贊相，太子識之。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was invested, Yuanheng assisted in the ceremony; the Heir Apparent recognized him.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was invested, Yuanheng assisted in the ceremony, and the Heir Apparent came to know him.

sentences.zh: 及即位，是為憲宗，復拜中丞，進戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne—he was Xianzong—Yuanheng was again appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief and promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne as Emperor Xianzong, Yuanheng was again appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief and promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 元和二年，拜門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事，兼判戶部事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhe, he was appointed Vice Minister of the Chancellery, Co-Deputy Director of the Chancellery with concurrent portfolio as chief minister, and concurrently managed Revenue Bureau affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanhe, he was appointed Vice Minister of the Chancellery, Co-Deputy Director of the Chancellery with concurrent portfolio as chief minister, with concurrent charge of Revenue Bureau affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝素知元衡堅正有守，故眷禮信任異它相。

translations.literal: The emperor had long known Yuanheng to be upright and principled, so he favored and trusted him differently from other chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long known Yuanheng to be upright and principled, and so favored and trusted him as he did no other chief minister.

sentences.zh: 浙西李锜求入覲，既又稱疾，欲賒其期。

translations.literal: Li Qi of Zhexi requested permission to come to court for an audience; then he claimed illness and sought to defer the date.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi of Zhexi asked to come to court for an audience, then claimed illness and sought to postpone the date.

sentences.zh: 帝問宰相鄭絪，絪請聽之，元衡曰：「不可，锜自請入朝，詔既許之，而復不至，是可否在锜。

translations.literal: The emperor asked chief minister Zheng Yin; Yin asked to allow it. Yuanheng said: "It cannot be done. Qi himself requested to come to court; the edict has already granted permission, yet he does not come. Whether this is permitted or not lies with Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked chief minister Zheng Yin, who asked to allow it. Yuanheng said, "That will not do. Qi himself requested to come to court; the edict has already granted permission, yet he does not come. Whether this is permitted or not is Qi's to decide.

sentences.zh: 陛下新即位，天下屬耳目，若奸臣得遂其私，則威令去矣。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty has newly ascended the throne; the realm watches with all its eyes and ears. If wicked ministers can have their way, authority and command will be lost."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has newly ascended the throne, and the realm watches with all its eyes and ears. If wicked ministers can have their way, imperial authority will be lost."

sentences.zh: 帝然之，遽追锜。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed and immediately ordered Qi to report.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and immediately ordered Qi to report to court.

sentences.zh: 而锜計窮，果反。

translations.literal: Qi, his stratagems exhausted, did indeed rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, his stratagems exhausted, did rebel.

sentences.zh: 是時，蜀新定，高崇文為節度，不知吏治，帝難其代。

translations.literal: At that time Shu had just been pacified. Gao Chongwen served as military commissioner but did not understand civil administration; the emperor found it difficult to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shu had just been pacified. Gao Chongwen served as military commissioner but knew nothing of civil administration, and the emperor found it difficult to replace him.

sentences.zh: 詔元衡檢校吏部尚書，兼門下侍郎、同平章事，為劍南西川節度使，繇蕭縣伯封臨淮郡公，帝禦安福門慰遣之。

translations.literal: Yuanheng was ordered appointed Acting Minister of Civil Appointments, concurrently Vice Minister of the Chancellery and Co-Deputy Director with concurrent portfolio as chief minister, and military commissioner of Jiannan West Circuit; he was enfeoffed from Baron of Xiao County to Duke of Linhuai County. The emperor went to Anfu Gate to console and send him off.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanheng was ordered appointed Acting Minister of Civil Appointments, concurrently Vice Minister of the Chancellery and Co-Deputy Director with concurrent portfolio as chief minister, and military commissioner of Jiannan West Circuit. He was enfeoffed from Baron of Xiao County to Duke of Linhuai County, and the emperor went to Anfu Gate to console and send him off.

sentences.zh: 崇文去成都，盡以金帛、帟幕、伎樂、工巧行，蜀幾為空。

translations.literal: When Chongwen left Chengdu, he took away all gold, silk, curtains, entertainers, and skilled artisans; Shu was nearly emptied.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongwen left Chengdu, he carried off all its gold, silk, hangings, entertainers, and skilled artisans, and Shu was nearly emptied.

sentences.zh: 元衡至，綏靖約束，儉己寬民，比三年，上下完實，蠻夷懷歸。

translations.literal: When Yuanheng arrived, he pacified and imposed order, was frugal in his own conduct and lenient toward the people. Within about three years, upper and lower levels were sound and full; the tribes submitted in longing to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanheng arrived, he pacified the region and imposed order, living frugally himself and treating the people leniently. Within about three years, government and populace alike were secure and prosperous, and the frontier tribes submitted willingly.

sentences.zh: 雅性莊重，雖淡於接物，而開府極一時選。

translations.literal: By nature he was solemn and dignified; though distant in receiving people, when he opened his staff he selected the finest men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was solemn and dignified. Though reserved in his dealings with others, when he opened his staff he chose the finest men of the age.

sentences.zh: 八年，召還秉政。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was recalled to assume government.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was recalled to take charge of the government.

sentences.zh: 李吉甫、李絳數爭事帝前，不葉，元衡獨持正無所違附，帝稱其長者。

translations.literal: Li Jifu and Li Jiang often argued over matters before the emperor without agreement; Yuanheng alone held to what was right without leaning to either side, and the emperor called him an elder in character.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jifu and Li Jiang often disputed matters before the emperor without reaching agreement. Yuanheng alone held to what was right without siding with either, and the emperor called him a man of mature character.

sentences.zh: 吉甫卒，淮、蔡用兵，帝悉以機政委之。

translations.literal: When Jifu died, as troops were deployed against Huai and Cai, the emperor entrusted all strategic decisions to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jifu died, with war underway against Huai and Cai, the emperor entrusted all strategic decisions to him.

sentences.zh: 王承宗上疏請赦吳元濟，使人白事中書，悖慢不恭，元衡叱去。

translations.literal: Wang Chengzong submitted a memorial requesting amnesty for Wu Yuanji and sent a man to inform the Secretariat of affairs; the man was insolent and disrespectful, and Yuanheng rebuked and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengzong submitted a memorial requesting amnesty for Wu Yuanji and sent a man to report the matter to the Secretariat. The man was insolent and disrespectful, and Yuanheng rebuked him and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 承宗怨，數上章誣詆。

translations.literal: Chengzong bore resentment and repeatedly submitted memorials slandering him.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong resented this and repeatedly submitted memorials slandering him.

sentences.zh: 未幾入朝，出靖安裏第，夜漏未盡，賊乘暗呼曰：「滅燭！」

translations.literal: Before long he came to court; leaving his residence in Jing'an Lane before the night watch had ended, assailants took advantage of the darkness and shouted: "Put out the candles!"
translations.idiomatic: Before long he came to court. Leaving his residence in Jing'an Lane before the night watch had ended, assailants took advantage of the darkness and shouted, "Put out the candles!"

sentences.zh: 射元衡中肩，復擊其左股，徒禦格鬥不勝，皆駭走，遂害元衡，批顱骨持去。

translations.literal: They shot Yuanheng in the shoulder, then struck his left thigh. His attendants fought but could not prevail; all fled in terror. They then killed Yuanheng, sliced off his skull, and carried it away.
translations.idiomatic: They shot Yuanheng in the shoulder, then struck his left thigh. His attendants fought but could not prevail and fled in terror. They then killed Yuanheng, sliced off his skull, and carried it away.

sentences.zh: 邏司傳噪盜殺宰相，連十餘里，達朝堂，百官恟懼，未知主名。

translations.literal: The patrol relay spread the clamor that bandits had killed a chief minister for more than ten li, reaching the court hall. All officials were alarmed and fearful, not knowing the victim's name.
translations.idiomatic: The patrol relay spread word that bandits had killed a chief minister, the clamor continuing for more than ten li until it reached the court hall. All officials were alarmed and fearful, not knowing who had been killed.

sentences.zh: 少選，馬逸還第，中外乃審知。

translations.literal: After a short while, his horse ran back to his residence, and then within and without the court all knew for certain.
translations.idiomatic: After a short while his horse ran back to his residence, and then court and capital alike knew for certain.

sentences.zh: 是日，仗入紫宸門，有司以聞，帝震驚，罷朝，坐延英見宰相，哀慟，為再不食。

translations.literal: That day, as the imperial guard entered Zichen Gate, the authorities reported it. The emperor was shaken, dismissed court, and received the chief ministers in Yan Ying Hall. He grieved in anguish and twice went without food.
translations.idiomatic: That day, as the imperial guard entered Zichen Gate, the authorities reported what had happened. The emperor was shaken, dismissed court, and received the chief ministers in Yan Ying Hall. Grieving in anguish, he twice went without food.

sentences.zh: 贈司徒，謚曰忠湣。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor and given the posthumous title Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor and given the posthumous title Loyal and Sorrowful.

sentences.zh: 詔金吾、府、縣大索，或傳言曰：「無搜賊，賊窮必亂。」

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Gold Guard, prefectural office, and county to search extensively. Some spread a rumor saying: "Do not search for the bandits; when bandits are cornered they will surely cause disorder."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Gold Guard, the prefectural office, and the counties to conduct a thorough search. Some spread a rumor: "Do not search for the bandits; when bandits are cornered they will surely cause disorder."

sentences.zh: 又投書於道曰：「毋急我，我先殺汝。」

translations.literal: Others cast letters on the road saying: "Do not press me; I will kill you first."
translations.idiomatic: Others cast letters on the road saying, "Do not press me; I will kill you first."

sentences.zh: 故吏卒不窮捕。

translations.literal: Therefore the clerks and soldiers did not hunt them to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, the clerks and soldiers did not pursue the bandits to the end.

sentences.zh: 兵部侍郎許孟容言於帝曰：「國相橫屍路隅而盜不獲，為朝廷辱。」

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War Xu Mengrong said to the emperor: "The state minister lies dead at a roadside corner while the bandits go uncaught—this is a disgrace to the court."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of War Xu Mengrong said to the emperor, "The state minister lies dead at a roadside corner while the bandits go uncaught. This is a disgrace to the court."

sentences.zh: 帝乃下詔：「能得賊者賞錢千萬，授五品官。

translations.literal: The emperor then issued an edict: "Whoever can capture the bandits shall be rewarded with ten million cash and granted a fifth-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then issued an edict: "Whoever captures the bandits shall be rewarded with ten million cash and granted a fifth-rank office.

sentences.zh: 與賊謀及舍賊能自言者亦賞。

translations.literal: Those who conspired with the bandits, or who sheltered them but can confess of their own accord, shall also be rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Those who conspired with the bandits, or who sheltered them but confess of their own accord, shall also be rewarded.

sentences.zh: 有不如詔，族之。」

translations.literal: Whoever does not comply with the edict shall have his clan exterminated."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever fails to comply with the edict shall have his entire clan exterminated."

sentences.zh: 積錢東西市以募告者。

translations.literal: Cash was piled in the East and West Markets to recruit informants.
translations.idiomatic: Cash was piled in the East and West Markets to recruit informants.

sentences.zh: 於是左神策將軍王士則、左威衛將軍王士平以賊聞，捕得張晏等十八人，言為承宗所遣，皆斬之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Left Shence General Wang Shize and Left Weiwu General Wang Shiping reported the bandits; Zhang Yan and eighteen others were captured. They said they had been sent by Chengzong, and all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Left Shence General Wang Shize and Left Weiwu General Wang Shiping reported the bandits. Zhang Yan and eighteen others were captured; they said they had been sent by Chengzong, and all were executed.

sentences.zh: 逾月，東都防禦使呂元膺執淄青留邸賊門察、訾嘉珍，自言始謀殺元衡者，會晏先發，故藉之以告師道而竊其賞，帝密誅之。

translations.literal: More than a month later, Eastern Capital Defense Commissioner Lu Yuanying arrested the Ziqing lodging house bandits Men Cha and Zi Jiazhen. They confessed that they had originally plotted to kill Yuanheng, but as Yan had acted first, they had used that to inform Shi Daodao and steal the reward. The emperor secretly executed them.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month later, Eastern Capital Defense Commissioner Lu Yuanying arrested the Ziqing lodging-house bandits Men Cha and Zi Jiazhen. They confessed that they had originally plotted to kill Yuanheng, but as Yan had acted first, they had used that to inform Shi Daodao and steal the reward. The emperor had them secretly executed.

sentences.zh: 初，京師大恐，城門加兵誰何，其偉狀異服、燕趙言者，皆驗訊乃遣。

translations.literal: At first the capital was greatly terrified. Troops were added at the city gates for scrutiny; those of imposing stature, unusual dress, or Yan-Zhao speech were all interrogated before being allowed to pass.
translations.idiomatic: At first the capital was gripped by terror. Extra troops were posted at the city gates for scrutiny; anyone of imposing stature, unusual dress, or Yan-Zhao accent was interrogated before being allowed to pass.

sentences.zh: 公卿朝，以家奴持兵呵衛，宰相則金吾彀騎導翼，每過裏門，搜索喧嘩。

translations.literal: When grandees attended court, they had household slaves bearing arms as guards. Chief ministers had Gold Guard armored horsemen escorting them on either side; at every lane gate searches raised a clamor.
translations.idiomatic: When grandees attended court, they had household slaves bearing arms as escorts. Chief ministers were flanked by Gold Guard armored horsemen, and at every lane gate searches raised a clamor.

sentences.zh: 因詔寅漏上二刻乃傳點雲。

translations.literal: Accordingly an edict was issued that the watch at the third quarter of the night should not signal the morning bell until two more clepsydra marks had passed.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly an edict was issued delaying the morning bell by two clepsydra marks beyond the third quarter of the night watch.

sentences.zh: 從父弟儒衡。

translations.literal: His paternal cousin Ruheng.
translations.idiomatic: His paternal cousin Ruheng.

sentences.zh: 儒衡，字廷碩，姿狀秀偉，不妄言，與人交，終始一節。

translations.literal: Ruheng, style name Tingshuo, was handsome and imposing in bearing. He did not speak rashly; in dealings with others he maintained one consistent principle from start to finish.
translations.idiomatic: Ruheng, courtesy name Tingshuo, was handsome and imposing in bearing. He did not speak rashly, and in his dealings with others he maintained one consistent principle from beginning to end.

sentences.zh: 宰相鄭餘慶不事華潔，門下客多垢衣敗服，獨儒衡上謁，未嘗有所易，以莊詞正色見重於餘慶。

translations.literal: Chief minister Zheng Yuqing did not favor elegance and ornament; most clients at his gate wore shabby, worn clothes. Only Ruheng, when paying calls, never changed his dress. With solemn words and upright bearing he was held in esteem by Yuqing.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Zheng Yuqing did not favor elegance and ornament, and most clients at his gate wore shabby, worn clothes. Only Ruheng, when paying calls, never altered his dress. With solemn words and upright bearing he won Yuqing's esteem.

sentences.zh: 元衡歿，帝待之益厚，累遷戶部郎中，知諫議大夫事，俄兼知制誥。

translations.literal: When Yuanheng died, the emperor treated him all the more generously, promoting him in succession to Director of the Revenue Bureau office, acting Remonstrance and Review Grand Counselor, and soon concurrently Drafting Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuanheng's death, the emperor treated him all the more generously, promoting him in succession to Director of the Revenue Bureau, acting Remonstrance and Review Grand Counselor, and soon concurrently Drafting Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 皇甫镈以宰相領度支，剝下以媚天子，儒衡疏其狀。

translations.literal: Huangfu Bo, as chief minister, also headed the Finance Commission and scraped the people to please the Son of Heaven. Ruheng memorialized exposing this.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Bo, serving as chief minister, also headed the Finance Commission and squeezed the people to please the emperor. Ruheng submitted a memorial exposing this.

sentences.zh: 镈自訴於帝，帝曰：「乃欲報怨邪？」

translations.literal: Bo complained to the emperor himself. The emperor said: "So you wish to settle a grudge, do you?"
translations.idiomatic: Bo complained to the emperor himself. The emperor said, "So you wish to settle a grudge, do you?"

sentences.zh: 镈不敢對。

translations.literal: Bo did not dare reply.
translations.idiomatic: Bo did not dare reply.

sentences.zh: 儒衡論議勁正，有風節，且將大用。

translations.literal: Ruheng's discourse was forceful and upright, with moral integrity, and he was about to be greatly employed.
translations.idiomatic: Ruheng's discourse was forceful and upright, and he had moral integrity; he was on the verge of high appointment.

sentences.zh: 宰相令狐楚忌之，會以狄兼謨為拾遺，楚自草制，引武后革命事，盛推仁傑功，以指切儒衡，且沮止之。

translations.literal: Chief minister Linghu Chu envied him. When Di Jianmo was appointed Reminder, Chu himself drafted the appointment edict, citing Empress Wu's seizure of power and lavishly praising Di Renjie's merit, to aim indirectly at Ruheng and obstruct his advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Linghu Chu envied him. When Di Jianmo was appointed Reminder, Chu himself drafted the appointment edict, citing Empress Wu's seizure of power and lavishly praising Di Renjie's merit, to aim indirectly at Ruheng and block his advancement.

sentences.zh: 儒衡泣見上曰：「臣祖平一，當天后時，避仕終老，不涉於累。」

translations.literal: Ruheng tearfully had an audience with the emperor and said: "My grandfather Pingyi, in Empress Wu's time, avoided office and ended his days in retirement, never entangled in imputation."
translations.idiomatic: Ruheng tearfully had an audience with the emperor and said, "My grandfather Pingyi, in Empress Wu's time, avoided office and lived out his days in retirement, never entangled in scandal."

sentences.zh: 帝慰勉之，自是薄楚為人也。

translations.literal: The emperor consoled and encouraged him. From then on he thought less of Chu as a man.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consoled and encouraged him. From then on he thought less of Chu as a man.

sentences.zh: 遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 時元稹倚宦官，知制誥，儒衡鄙厭之。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Zhen relied on eunuchs and served as Drafting Secretariat; Ruheng despised and loathed him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuan Zhen relied on eunuchs and served as Drafting Secretariat; Ruheng despised him.

sentences.zh: 會食瓜，蠅集其上，儒衡揮以扇，曰：「適從何處來，遽集於此？」

translations.literal: Once while eating melon, flies gathered on it. Ruheng waved them away with a fan and said: "Whence did you just come, that you suddenly cluster here?"
translations.idiomatic: Once while eating melon, flies gathered on it. Ruheng waved them away with a fan and said, "Whence did you just come, that you suddenly cluster here?"

sentences.zh: 一坐皆失色。

translations.literal: All present turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: All present turned pale.

sentences.zh: 然以疾惡太分明，終不至大任，以兵部侍郎卒，年五十六，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: Yet because his hatred of evil was too sharply drawn, he never reached high office. He died as Vice Minister of War at age fifty-six and was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because his hatred of evil was too sharply drawn, he never reached high office. He died as Vice Minister of War at the age of fifty-six and was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 李絳，字深之，系本贊皇。

translations.literal: Li Jiang, style name Shenzhi, was descended from Zanhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang, courtesy name Shenzhi, traced his lineage to Zanhuang.

sentences.zh: 擢進士、宏辭，補渭南尉，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi and comprehensive literary examinations, was appointed assistant magistrate of Weinan, and appointed Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi and comprehensive literary examinations, was appointed assistant magistrate of Weinan, and was made Palace Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 元和二年，授翰林學士，俄知制誥。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhe he was appointed Hanlin Academician; soon he was placed in charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanhe he was appointed Hanlin Academician and soon placed in charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 會李锜誅，憲宗將輦取其貲，絳與裴垍諫曰：「锜僭侈誅求，六州之人怨入骨髓。

translations.literal: When Li Qi was executed, Xianzong intended to have his wealth carted away. Jiang and Pei Ji remonstrated, saying: "Qi was extravagant and oppressive in exactions; the people of six prefectures hated him to the marrow.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Qi was executed, Emperor Xianzong intended to have his wealth carted away. Jiang and Pei Ji remonstrated, saying, "Qi was extravagant and oppressive in his exactions; the people of six prefectures hated him to the marrow.

sentences.zh: 今元惡傳首，若因取其財，恐非遏亂略、惠綏困窮者。

translations.literal: Now that the chief villain's head has been sent, if we take his wealth on that account, I fear this is not the way to restrain rebellion and banditry and to succor the distressed and impoverished.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the chief villain's head has been sent, if we seize his wealth on that account, I fear this is not the way to restrain rebellion or succor the distressed and impoverished.

sentences.zh: 願賜本道，代貧民租賦。」

translations.literal: We ask that it be granted to his circuit to cover the tax and corvée of the poor."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that it be granted to his circuit to cover the tax and corvée levies of the poor."

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 樞密使劉光琦議遣中人持赦令賜諸道，以裒饋餉，絳請付度支鹽鐵急遞以遣，息取求之弊。

translations.literal: Privy Envoy Liu Guangqi proposed sending palace envoys to carry amnesty edicts to the various circuits to collect provisions. Jiang asked that this be entrusted to the Finance Commission and Salt and Iron Bureau's express relay to dispatch them, to end the evils of extortion.
translations.idiomatic: Privy Envoy Liu Guangqi proposed sending palace envoys to carry amnesty edicts to the various circuits to collect provisions. Jiang asked that the task be entrusted to the Finance Commission and Salt and Iron Bureau's express relay, to end the evils of extortion.

sentences.zh: 光琦引故事以對，帝曰：「故事是耶，當守之；

translations.literal: Guangqi cited precedent in reply. The emperor said: "If precedent is correct, it should be kept;
translations.idiomatic: Guangqi cited precedent in reply. The emperor said, "If precedent is correct, it should be kept;

sentences.zh: 不然，當改。

translations.literal: if not, it should be changed.
translations.idiomatic: if not, it should be changed.

sentences.zh: 可循舊哉！」

translations.literal: How can one simply follow the old ways!"
translations.idiomatic: How can one simply follow the old ways!"

sentences.zh: 帝嘗稱太宗、玄宗之盛：「朕不佞，欲庶幾二祖之道德風烈，無愧謚號，不為宗廟羞，何行而至此乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor once praised the greatness of Taizong and Xuanzong: "I am not clever, yet I wish to approach the moral virtue and majestic example of the two founders, not unworthy of their posthumous titles and not shaming the ancestral temple—by what conduct can one reach this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once praised the greatness of Taizong and Xuanzong: "I am not clever, yet I wish to approach the moral virtue and majestic example of the two founders, not unworthy of their posthumous titles and not shaming the ancestral temple—by what conduct can one reach this?"

sentences.zh: 絳曰：「陛下誠能正身勵己，尊道德，遠邪佞，進忠直。

translations.literal: Jiang said: "If Your Majesty can truly correct your person and exhort yourself, honor moral virtue, keep the wicked and fawning at a distance, and advance the loyal and upright—
translations.idiomatic: Jiang said, "If Your Majesty can truly correct your person and exhort yourself, honor moral virtue, keep the wicked and fawning at a distance, and advance the loyal and upright—

sentences.zh: 與大臣言，敬而信，無使小人參焉；

translations.literal: in speaking with grand ministers, be respectful and trusting, and do not let petty men participate;
translations.idiomatic: in speaking with grand ministers, be respectful and trusting, and do not let petty men participate;

sentences.zh: 與賢者遊，親而禮，無使不肖與焉。

translations.literal: in keeping company with the worthy, be intimate yet courteous, and do not let the unworthy join in.
translations.idiomatic: in keeping company with the worthy, be intimate yet courteous, and do not let the unworthy join in.

sentences.zh: 去官無益於治者，則材能出；

translations.literal: Remove officials who do no good for governance, and talent will emerge;
translations.idiomatic: Remove officials who do no good for governance, and talent will emerge;

sentences.zh: 斥宮女之希禦者，則怨曠銷。

translations.literal: dismiss palace women who hope for imperial favor, and grievances from separation will dissolve.
translations.idiomatic: dismiss palace women who hope for imperial favor, and grievances from enforced separation will dissolve.

sentences.zh: 將帥擇，士卒勇矣；

translations.literal: Choose generals well, and the soldiers will be brave;
translations.idiomatic: Choose generals well, and the soldiers will be brave;

sentences.zh: 官師公，吏治輯矣。

translations.literal: make officers and teachers impartial, and civil administration will be orderly.
translations.idiomatic: make officers and teachers impartial, and civil administration will be orderly.

sentences.zh: 法令行而下不違，教化篤而俗必遷。

translations.literal: When laws and orders are carried out and subordinates do not violate them, when instruction is sincere, custom will surely change.
translations.idiomatic: When laws and orders are carried out and subordinates do not violate them, when instruction is sincere, custom will surely change.

sentences.zh: 如是，可與祖宗合德，號稱中興，夫何遠之有？

translations.literal: In this way one can join in virtue with the ancestors and be called a restoration—how far off could it be?
translations.idiomatic: In this way one can join in virtue with the ancestors and be called a restoration—how far off could that be?

sentences.zh: 言之不行，無益也；

translations.literal: To speak without acting is of no benefit;
translations.idiomatic: To speak without acting is of no benefit;

sentences.zh: 行之不至，無益也。」

translations.literal: to act without reaching the goal is of no benefit."
translations.idiomatic: to act without reaching the goal is of no benefit."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「美哉斯言，朕將書諸紳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How fine these words! I shall write them on my belt sash."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "How fine these words! I shall write them on my belt sash."

sentences.zh: 即詔絳與崔群、錢徽、韋弘景、白居易等搜次君臣成敗五十種，為連屏，張便坐。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered Jiang, together with Cui Qun, Qian Hui, Wei Hongjing, Bai Juyi, and others to compile fifty accounts of success and failure among rulers and ministers, made them into linked screens, and hung them in the informal audience hall.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered Jiang, together with Cui Qun, Qian Hui, Wei Hongjing, Bai Juyi, and others, to compile fifty accounts of success and failure among rulers and ministers, made them into linked screens, and hung them in the informal audience hall.

sentences.zh: 帝每閱視，顧左右曰：「而等宜作意，勿為如此事。」

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor reviewed them, he would turn to those beside him and say: "You should take heed—do not do such things."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor reviewed them, he would turn to those beside him and say, "You should take heed—do not do such things."

sentences.zh: 是時，盛興安國佛祠，幸臣吐突承璀請立石紀聖德焉，營構華廣，欲使絳為之頌，將遺錢千萬。

translations.literal: At that time the Anguo Buddhist temple was flourishing. The favorite Tu Tuchengcui requested that a stele be erected to record the sage virtue; construction was magnificent and extensive. He wished to have Jiang compose its encomium and was about to present ten million cash.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Anguo Buddhist temple was flourishing. The favorite Tu Tuchengcui requested that a stele be erected to record the sage virtue. Construction was magnificent and extensive, and he wished to have Jiang compose its encomium, offering ten million cash.

sentences.zh: 絳上言：「陛下蕩積習之弊，四海延頸望德音，忽自立碑，示人以不廣。

translations.literal: Jiang submitted: "Your Majesty has swept away accumulated abuses; the four seas stretch their necks awaiting words of virtue. Suddenly to erect a stele yourself shows the people a lack of breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang submitted: "Your Majesty has swept away accumulated abuses; the four seas stretch their necks awaiting words of virtue. Suddenly to erect a stele yourself shows the people a lack of breadth.

sentences.zh: 《易》稱：『大人與天地合德。』

translations.literal: The Changes says: 'The great man joins in virtue with Heaven and Earth.'
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says: 'The great man joins in virtue with Heaven and Earth.'

sentences.zh: 謂非文字所能盡，若令可述，是陛下美有分限。

translations.literal: This means it cannot be fully expressed in writing. If your command can be narrated, then Your Majesty's excellence has a limit.
translations.idiomatic: This means it cannot be fully expressed in writing. If your command can be narrated, then Your Majesty's excellence has a limit.

sentences.zh: 堯、舜至文、武，皆不傳其事，惟秦始刻嶧山，揚暴誅伐巡幸之勞，失道之君，不足為法。

translations.literal: From Yao and Shun down to Wen and Wu, none transmitted their deeds in this way. Only the First Emperor of Qin carved Mount Yi, proclaiming the labors of violent punishment, conquest, and imperial tours—a ruler who lost the Way, not fit to be a model.
translations.idiomatic: From Yao and Shun down to Wen and Wu, none transmitted their deeds in this way. Only the First Emperor of Qin carved Mount Yi, proclaiming the labors of violent punishment, conquest, and imperial tours—a ruler who lost the Way, unfit to be a model.

sentences.zh: 今安國有碑，若敘遊觀，即非治要；

translations.literal: Now if the Anguo stele narrates sightseeing, it is not a priority of governance;
translations.idiomatic: Now if the Anguo stele narrates sightseeing, it is not a priority of governance;

sentences.zh: 述崇飾，又非政宜。

translations.literal: if it describes grandeur and ornament, it is again unsuitable for government.
translations.idiomatic: if it describes grandeur and ornament, it is again unsuitable for government.

sentences.zh: 請罷之。」

translations.literal: I ask that it be stopped."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that it be stopped."

sentences.zh: 帝怒，絳伏奏愈切，帝悟曰：「微絳，我不自知。」

translations.literal: The emperor was angry. Jiang prostrated himself and remonstrated all the more urgently. The emperor came to understand and said: "But for Jiang, I would not have known myself."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry. Jiang prostrated himself and remonstrated all the more urgently. The emperor came to understand and said, "But for Jiang, I would not have known myself."

sentences.zh: 命百牛倒石，令使者勞諭絳。

translations.literal: He ordered a hundred oxen to pull down the stone and sent an envoy to console and commend Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a hundred oxen to pull down the stone and sent an envoy to console and commend Jiang.

sentences.zh: 襄陽裴均違詔書，獻銀壺甕數百具，絳請歸之度支，示天下以信。

translations.literal: Pei Jun of Xiangyang violated an edict and presented several hundred silver jars and urns. Jiang asked that they be returned to the Finance Commission to show the realm good faith.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Jun of Xiangyang violated an edict and presented several hundred silver jars and urns. Jiang asked that they be returned to the Finance Commission to show the realm that the court keeps its word.

sentences.zh: 帝可奏，仍赦均罪。

translations.literal: The emperor approved the memorial and also pardoned Jun's offense.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the memorial and also pardoned Jun's offense.

sentences.zh: 時議還盧從史昭義，已而將復召之，從史以軍無見儲為解。

translations.literal: At the time there was discussion of returning Lu Congshi to Zhaoyi. Soon he was to be summoned again; Congshi excused himself on the grounds that the army had no provisions on hand.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was discussion of returning Lu Congshi to Zhaoyi. Soon he was to be summoned again, but Congshi excused himself on the grounds that the army had no provisions on hand.

sentences.zh: 李吉甫謂鄭絪漏其謀，帝召絳議，欲逐絪，絳為開白，乃免。

translations.literal: Li Jifu said Zheng Yin had leaked their plan. The emperor summoned Jiang to discuss it and intended to expel Yin. Jiang spoke in his defense, and Yin was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jifu said Zheng Yin had leaked their plan. The emperor summoned Jiang to discuss it and intended to expel Yin. Jiang spoke in Yin's defense, and Yin was spared.

sentences.zh: 絳見浴堂殿，帝曰：「比諫官多朋黨，論奏不實，皆陷謗訕，欲黜其尤者，若何？」

translations.literal: Jiang had an audience at the Bath Hall. The emperor said: "Lately remonstrance officials form many factions; their memorials and reports are untrue and all descend into slander—I wish to dismiss the worst offenders. What do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiang had an audience at the Bath Hall. The emperor said, "Lately remonstrance officials form many factions; their memorials and reports are untrue and all descend into slander. I wish to dismiss the worst offenders. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 絳曰：「此非陛下意，必憸人以此營誤上心。

translations.literal: Jiang said: "This is not Your Majesty's intent—it must be sly men using this scheme to mislead the emperor's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang said, "This is not Your Majesty's intent. Sly men must be using this scheme to mislead your heart.

sentences.zh: 自古納諫昌，拒諫亡。

translations.literal: From antiquity, accepting remonstrance brings prosperity; rejecting remonstrance brings ruin.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity, states that accepted remonstrance prospered, and those that rejected it perished.

sentences.zh: 夫人臣進言於上，豈易哉？

translations.literal: For a minister to speak forth to his superior—how is it easy?
translations.idiomatic: For a minister to speak forth to his sovereign—how could it be easy?

sentences.zh: 君尊如天，臣卑如地，加有雷霆之威，彼晝度夜思，始欲陳十事，俄而去五六，及將以聞，則又憚而削其半，故上達者財十二。

translations.literal: The lord is lofty as heaven, the minister lowly as earth, and on top of this there is the awe of thunder. They measure by day and think by night: at first they mean to set forth ten matters, but soon five or six are dropped; when they are about to report, they again fear and cut off half—thus what reaches the top is barely one or two in ten.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign is lofty as heaven and the minister lowly as earth, and on top of that there is the awe of thunder. They reckon by day and brood by night: at first they mean to set forth ten matters, but soon five or six fall away; when they are about to speak, fear cuts the rest in half—so barely one or two in ten ever reach the throne.

sentences.zh: 何哉？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 幹不測之禍，顧身無利耳。

translations.literal: They risk unforeseeable calamity and consider that they themselves gain nothing.
translations.idiomatic: They risk unforeseeable disaster while gaining nothing for themselves.

sentences.zh: 雖開納獎勵，尚恐不至，今乃欲譴訶之，使直士杜口，非社稷利也。」

translations.literal: Even with open welcome and reward for remonstrance, one still fears that none will come forth—yet now you wish to rebuke and reproach them, making upright men seal their lips. This is not to the state's benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Even with open welcome and rewards for remonstrance, one still fears that none will come forward—yet now you wish to rebuke and reproach them and make upright men seal their lips. That is not to the state's benefit."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「非卿言，我不知諫之益。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "But for your words, I would not have known the benefit of remonstrance."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "But for your words, I would not have known the benefit of remonstrance."

sentences.zh: 初，承璀討王承宗，議者皆言古無以宦人統師者，絳當制書，固爭，帝不能奪，止詔宰相授敕。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Cheng Cui was campaigning against Wang Chengzong, debaters all said that in antiquity there was never a eunuch commanding armies. Jiang was responsible for drafting the edict and firmly remonstrated. The emperor could not override him and stopped at ordering the chief ministers to deliver the commission.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Cheng Cui was campaigning against Wang Chengzong, critics all said that antiquity knew no eunuch commanding armies. Jiang was charged with drafting the edict and remonstrated firmly. The emperor could not override him and stopped at ordering the chief ministers to deliver the commission.

sentences.zh: 承璀果無功還，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Cheng Cui indeed returned without achievement and was promoted to Grand Guardian with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Cui indeed returned without success and was promoted to Grand Guardian with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 絳奏：「承璀喪師，當抵罪，今寵以崇秩，後有奔軍之將，蹈利幹賞，陛下何以處之？」

translations.literal: Jiang memorialized: "Cheng Cui lost his army and should be punished; now he is favored with exalted rank. Later, when there are generals who flee battle and rush for profit to seek reward, how will Your Majesty deal with them?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiang memorialized, "Cheng Cui lost his army and should be punished, yet now he is favored with exalted rank. Later, when generals flee battle and rush for profit to seek reward, how will Your Majesty deal with them?"

sentences.zh: 又數論宦官橫肆，方鎮進獻等事。

translations.literal: He also repeatedly argued about eunuchs' wanton license and the tribute offerings of regional commanders, among other matters.
translations.idiomatic: He also repeatedly argued about the wanton license of eunuchs, the tribute offerings of regional commanders, and other such matters.

sentences.zh: 自知言切，且斥去，悉取內署所上疏稿焚之，以俟命。

translations.literal: Knowing his words were cutting and that he might soon be dismissed, he gathered all draft memorials he had submitted in the inner secretariat and burned them, then awaited his fate.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing his words were sharp and that he might soon be dismissed, he gathered all draft memorials he had submitted in the inner secretariat, burned them, and awaited his fate.

sentences.zh: 帝果怒，絳謝曰：「陛下憐臣愚，處之腹心之地，而惜身不言，乃臣負陛下；

translations.literal: The emperor was indeed angry. Jiang apologized, saying: "Your Majesty took pity on my dullness and placed me in the seat of your innermost trust. If I valued my person and did not speak, then I failed Your Majesty;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was indeed angry. Jiang apologized, saying, "Your Majesty took pity on my dullness and placed me in the seat of your innermost trust. If I prized my safety and did not speak, then I failed Your Majesty;

sentences.zh: 若上犯聖顏，旁忤貴幸，因而獲罪，乃陛下負臣。」

translations.literal: if by offending Your Majesty's countenance and going against powerful favorites I thereby suffer punishment, then Your Majesty failed me."
translations.idiomatic: if by offending Your Majesty's countenance and going against powerful favorites I suffer punishment, then Your Majesty failed me."

sentences.zh: 於是帝動容曰：「卿告朕以人所難言者，疾風知勁草，卿當之矣。」

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor was moved and said: "You have told me what others find hard to say. 'Strong winds reveal tough grass'—you have met the test."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the emperor was moved and said, "You have told me what others find hard to say. 'Strong winds reveal tough grass'—you have met the test."

sentences.zh: 遂繇司勛郎中進中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was then promoted from Director in the Bureau of Merits to Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted from director in the Bureau of Merits to drafting secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 翌日，賜金紫，親擇良笏與之，且曰：「異時膺顧托南面，當如此。」

translations.literal: The next day, he was granted gold seal and purple robe; the emperor personally chose a fine court tablet and gave it to him, saying: "When you later receive the trust of rule and face south as sovereign, it should be like this."
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was granted the gold seal and purple robe. The emperor personally chose a fine court tablet and gave it to him, saying, "When you later receive the trust of rule and face south as sovereign, it should be like this."

sentences.zh: 絳頓首。

translations.literal: Jiang bowed his head to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang bowed his head to the ground.

sentences.zh: 烏重胤縛盧從史，而承璀牒署昭義留後，絳曰：「澤潞據山東要害，磁、邢、洺跨兩河間，可制其合從。

translations.literal: Wu Chongyin bound Lu Congshi, while Cheng Cui by memorandum appointed the acting commander of Zhaoyi. Jiang said: "Ze-Lu occupies the strategic points of Shandong; Ci, Xing, and Ming span the space between the two He regions and can check their alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chongyin bound Lu Congshi, while Cheng Cui by memorandum appointed the acting commander of Zhaoyi. Jiang said, "Ze-Lu occupies the strategic points of Shandong; Ci, Xing, and Ming span the space between the two He regions and can check their alliance.

sentences.zh: 今孽豎就禽，方收威柄，遽以偏將蒞本軍，綱紀大紊矣。
