translations.literal: Now that the evil upstart has been captured and authority is just being reclaimed, abruptly to send a subordinate general to take command of the army itself—regulations will be greatly thrown into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the evil upstart has been captured and authority is just being reclaimed, to send a subordinate general abruptly to take command of the army itself will throw discipline into great disorder.

sentences.zh: 河南、北諸鎮，謂陛下啗以官爵，使逐其帥，其肯默然哉？

translations.literal: The various commands north and south of the Yellow River will think Your Majesty is baiting them with offices and titles to make them drive out their commanders—will they keep silent?
translations.idiomatic: The various commands north and south of the Yellow River will think Your Majesty is baiting them with offices and titles to make them drive out their commanders—will they keep silent?

sentences.zh: 宜以孟元陽為澤潞，而以重胤節度三城，兩河諸侯聞之，必欣然。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to appoint Meng Yuanyang over Ze-Lu and make Chongyin military commissioner of the three prefectures. When the lords of the two He regions hear this, they will surely be pleased."
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting to appoint Meng Yuanyang over Ze-Lu and make Chongyin military commissioner of the three prefectures. When the lords of the two He regions hear this, they will surely be pleased."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed this advice.

sentences.zh: 張茂昭舉族入覲，絳上言：「任迪簡既往代，則士之從茂昭，皆為定人，宜亟授以官，且遣使者詔其麾下皆聽茂昭節度。」

translations.literal: Zhang Maozhao brought his whole clan to court. Jiang submitted: "If Ren Dijian were allowed to remain in office, the men who followed Maozhao would all become settled personnel. He should promptly be granted office, and an envoy should be sent to command those under him to all obey Maozhao's command."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Maozhao brought his whole clan to court. Jiang submitted, "If Ren Dijian were allowed to remain in office, the men who followed Maozhao would all become settled personnel. He should promptly be granted office, and an envoy should be sent to command all under him to obey Maozhao's command."

sentences.zh: 有詔拜河中節度使。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him military commissioner of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him military commissioner of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 會迪簡以帑廥匱竭，稍簡罷士之疲老者，人情不安，迪簡亦危，絳請斥禁帑絹十萬以濟事機。

translations.literal: Just then Dijian, because the treasury and storehouses were exhausted, began gradually selecting and dismissing weary and aged soldiers. Morale was unsettled and Dijian himself was imperiled. Jiang asked that a hundred thousand bolts of silk from the forbidden treasury be released to meet the emergency.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Dijian, because the treasury and storehouses were exhausted, began gradually selecting and dismissing weary and aged soldiers. Morale was unsettled and Dijian himself was imperiled. Jiang asked that a hundred thousand bolts of silk from the forbidden treasury be released to meet the emergency.

sentences.zh: 吳少誠病甚，絳建言：「淮西地不與賊接，若朝廷命帥，今乃其時，有如阻命，則決可討矣。

translations.literal: Wu Shaocheng was gravely ill. Jiang proposed: "Huai-Xi's territory does not border the rebels. If the court appoints a commander, now is the time. Should anyone resist the order, then a punitive campaign can certainly be decided.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shaocheng was gravely ill. Jiang proposed, "Huai-Xi's territory does not border the rebels. If the court appoints a commander, now is the time. Should anyone resist the order, a punitive campaign can certainly be decided.

sentences.zh: 然鎮、蔡不可並取，願赦承宗，趣立蔡功。」

translations.literal: Yet Zhen and Cai cannot both be taken at once. I ask that Chengzong be pardoned and that effort be hastened to establish success at Cai."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhen and Cai cannot both be taken at once. I ask that Chengzong be pardoned and that effort be hastened to establish success at Cai."

sentences.zh: 時江淮大旱，帝下赦令有所蠲弛，絳言：「江淮流亡，所貸未廣，而宮人猥積，有怨鬲之思，當大出之，以省經費。

translations.literal: At the time the Jiang-Huai region suffered great drought. The emperor issued an amnesty with some remissions and relaxations. Jiang said: "Refugees are streaming through the Jiang-Huai, and relief granted is not broad enough, while palace women are piled up in great numbers, giving rise to resentful thoughts of separation. They should be released in large numbers to save state expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Jiang-Huai region suffered great drought. The emperor issued an amnesty with some remissions and relaxations. Jiang said, "Refugees are streaming through the Jiang-Huai, and relief granted is not broad enough, while palace women are piled up in great numbers, giving rise to resentful thoughts of separation. They should be released in large numbers to save state expenditure.

sentences.zh: 嶺南之俗，鬻子為業，可聽；

translations.literal: In the customs of Lingnan, selling children is a trade—this may be tolerated;
translations.idiomatic: In the customs of Lingnan, selling children is a trade—this may be tolerated;

sentences.zh: 非券劑取直者，如掠賣法，敕有司一切苛止。」

translations.literal: but where there is no contract or receipt for payment, treat it as abduction and sale by law, and order the authorities strictly to stop it altogether."
translations.idiomatic: but where there is no contract or receipt for payment, treat it as abduction and sale by law, and order the authorities strictly to stop it altogether."

sentences.zh: 帝皆順納。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted all of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted all of this.

sentences.zh: 後閱月不賜對，絳謂：「大臣持祿不敢諫，小臣畏罪不敢言，管仲以為害霸最甚。

translations.literal: After more than a month without being granted audience, Jiang said: "Great ministers hold salary but dare not remonstrate; lesser officials fear punishment and dare not speak. Guan Zhong regarded this as the greatest harm to hegemony.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month without being granted audience, Jiang said, "Great ministers hold salary but dare not remonstrate; lesser officials fear punishment and dare not speak. Guan Zhong regarded this as the greatest harm to hegemony.

sentences.zh: 今臣等飽食不言，無履危之患，自為計得矣，顧聖治如何？」

translations.literal: Now we are well fed and say nothing; we have no danger of treading on peril—fine for our private reckoning, but what of sagely governance?"
translations.idiomatic: Now we are well fed and say nothing; we have no danger of treading on peril—fine for our private reckoning, but what of sagely governance?"

sentences.zh: 有詔明日對三殿。

translations.literal: An edict ordered audience in the Three Halls the next day.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered audience in the Three Halls the next day.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗畋苑中，至蓬萊池，謂左右曰：「絳嘗以諫我，今可返也。」

translations.literal: Once when the emperor was hunting in the park and reached Penglai Pool, he said to those beside him: "Jiang once remonstrated with me about this—it is time to turn back.
translations.idiomatic: Once when the emperor was hunting in the park and reached Penglai Pool, he said to those beside him, "Jiang once remonstrated with me about this—it is time to turn back.

sentences.zh: 其見禮憚如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem and deference shown him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem and deference shown him.

sentences.zh: 帝怪前世任賢以致治，今無賢可任，何耶？

translations.literal: The emperor wondered that in former ages men appointed the worthy and thereby achieved good order, yet now there were no worthies to appoint—why?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wondered that in former ages rulers appointed the worthy and thereby achieved good order, yet now there were no worthies to appoint—why?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「聖王選當代之人，極其才分，自可致治。

translations.literal: He replied: "Sagely kings select men of their own age and bring their talents to their fullest limits—good order follows of itself.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Sagely kings select men of their own age and bring their talents to their fullest limits—good order follows of itself.

sentences.zh: 豈借賢異代，治今日之人哉？

translations.literal: How could one borrow worthies from another age to govern the people of today?
translations.idiomatic: How could one borrow worthies from another age to govern the people of today?

sentences.zh: 天子不以己能蓋人，痛折節下士，則天下賢者乃出。」

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven does not let his own abilities overshadow others and painfully bends his stature to defer to men below, then the worthies of the realm emerge."
translations.idiomatic: When the Son of Heaven does not let his own abilities overshadow others and painfully bends his stature to defer to men below, then the worthies of the realm emerge."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「何知其必賢而任之？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How does one know they are surely worthy and appoint them?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "How does one know they are surely worthy and appoint them?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「知人誠難，堯、舜以為病。

translations.literal: He replied: "Knowing men is truly difficult—even Yao and Shun regarded it as their affliction.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Knowing men is truly difficult—even Yao and Shun regarded it as their affliction.

sentences.zh: 然循其名，驗以事，所得十七。

translations.literal: Yet follow their reputation and test them by deeds, and you will obtain seven or eight out of ten.
translations.idiomatic: Yet follow their reputation and test them by deeds, and you will obtain seven or eight out of ten.

sentences.zh: 夫任官而辨廉，措事不阿容，無希望依違之辭，無邪媚愉悅之容，此近於賢矣。

translations.literal: When one holds office and distinguishes integrity, handles affairs without flattery, has no words of hopeful equivocation, and no countenance of wicked fawning pleasure—this approaches worthiness.
translations.idiomatic: When one holds office and distinguishes integrity, handles affairs without flattery, has no words of hopeful equivocation, and no countenance of wicked fawning pleasure—this approaches worthiness.

sentences.zh: 賢則當任，任則當久。

translations.literal: If worthy, then one should appoint; if appointed, then one should keep long.
translations.idiomatic: If worthy, then appoint; if appointed, then keep long.

sentences.zh: 賢者中立而寡助，舉其類則不肖者怨，杜邪徑則懷奸者疾，一制度則貴戚毀傷，正過失則人君疏忌。

translations.literal: The worthy stand in the middle with few helpers. Promote their kind and the unworthy resent it; block crooked paths and those harboring treachery hate it; unify regulations and noble kin are wounded; correct faults and the ruler grows distant and suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: The worthy stand in the middle with few helpers. Promote their kind and the unworthy resent it; block crooked paths and those harboring treachery hate it; unify regulations and noble kin are wounded; correct faults and the ruler grows distant and suspicious.

sentences.zh: 夫然，用賢豈容易哉？」

translations.literal: Thus, is employing the worthy easily done?"
translations.idiomatic: Thus, is employing the worthy easily done?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿言得之矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What you say hits the mark."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "What you say hits the mark."

sentences.zh: 六年，罷學士，遷戶部侍郎，判本司。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was removed as Hanlin Academician and transferred to Vice Director of the Revenue Ministry, with concurrent authority over that bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was removed as Hanlin Academician and transferred to vice director of the Revenue Ministry, with concurrent authority over that bureau.

sentences.zh: 帝以戶部故有獻，而絳獨無有，何哉？

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "The Revenue Ministry customarily has tribute offerings—why does Jiang alone have none?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "The Revenue Ministry customarily has tribute offerings—why does Jiang alone have none?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「凡方鎮有地則有賦，或嗇用度易羨余以為獻。

translations.literal: He replied: "Whenever a regional command has territory it has taxes. Some stint their expenditures and trade surplus for tribute offerings.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Whenever a regional command has territory it has taxes. Some stint their expenditures and trade surplus for tribute offerings.

sentences.zh: 臣乃為陛下謹出納，烏有羨贏哉？

translations.literal: I am simply careful in receipt and disbursement for Your Majesty—how could there be surplus profit?
translations.idiomatic: I am simply careful in receipt and disbursement for Your Majesty—how could there be surplus profit?

sentences.zh: 若以為獻，是徙東庫物實西庫，進官物結私恩。」

translations.literal: If these were offered as tribute, it would be moving goods from the eastern storehouse into the western storehouse—presenting official property to forge private favor."
translations.idiomatic: If these were offered as tribute, it would be moving goods from the eastern storehouse into the western storehouse—presenting official property to forge private favor."

sentences.zh: 帝瞿然悟。

translations.literal: The emperor started awake in sudden understanding.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started awake in sudden understanding.

sentences.zh: 帝每有詢訪，隨事補益，所言無不聽，欲遂以相。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor inquired of him, Jiang would add what was lacking according to the matter; nothing he said went unheeded, and the emperor wished to make him chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor inquired of him, Jiang would add what was lacking according to the matter; nothing he said went unheeded, and the emperor wished to make him chief minister.

sentences.zh: 而承璀寵方盛，忌其進，陰有毀短，帝乃出承璀淮南監軍。

translations.literal: But Cheng Cui's favor was then at its height; jealous of Jiang's advancement, he secretly slandered him. The emperor then sent Cheng Cui out as army supervisor at Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: But Cheng Cui's favor was then at its height; jealous of Jiang's advancement, he secretly slandered him. The emperor then sent Cheng Cui out as army supervisor at Huainan.

sentences.zh: 翌日，拜絳中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: The next day Jiang was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Jiang was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and concurrent grand councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 封高邑男。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoyi.

sentences.zh: 方江淮歲儉，民薦饑，有御史使還，奏不為災，帝以語絳，答曰：「方隅皆陛下大臣，奏孰不實？

translations.literal: Just then the Jiang-Huai year was lean and the people suffered repeated famine. A censor returning from a mission reported that there was no disaster. The emperor told Jiang, who replied: "The regions are all Your Majesty's chief ministers—whose reports are not truthful?
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Jiang-Huai year was lean and the people suffered repeated famine. A censor returning from a mission reported that there was no disaster. The emperor told Jiang, who replied, "The regions are all Your Majesty's chief ministers—whose reports are not truthful?

sentences.zh: 而御史茍悅陛下耳。

translations.literal: But the censor merely seeks to please Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: But the censor merely seeks to please Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 凡君人者當任大臣，無使小臣得以間，願出其名顯責之。」

translations.literal: For one who rules men, chief ministers should be entrusted and lesser officials must not be allowed to interfere. I ask that his name be published and he be openly censured."
translations.idiomatic: For one who rules men, chief ministers should be entrusted and lesser officials must not be allowed to interfere. I ask that his name be published and he be openly censured."

sentences.zh: 李吉甫嘗盛贊天子威德，帝欣然，絳獨曰：「陛下自視今日何如漢文帝時？」

translations.literal: Li Jifu once lavishly praised the Son of Heaven's majesty and virtue. The emperor was pleased, but Jiang alone said: "Does Your Majesty see today as comparable to the time of Emperor Wen of Han?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Jifu once lavishly praised the Son of Heaven's majesty and virtue. The emperor was pleased, but Jiang alone said, "Does Your Majesty see today as comparable to the time of Emperor Wen of Han?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕安敢望文帝？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How dare I compare myself to Emperor Wen?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "How dare I compare myself to Emperor Wen?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「是時賈誼以為措火積薪下，火未及然，因以為安，其憂如此。

translations.literal: He replied: "At that time Jia Yi said firewood was piled beneath a fire, the flame had not yet kindled, and yet they deemed themselves secure—such was his worry.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "At that time Jia Yi said firewood was piled beneath a fire, the flame had not yet kindled, and yet they deemed themselves secure—such was his worry.

sentences.zh: 今法令所不及者五十餘州，西戎內訌，近以涇、隴為鄙，去京師遠不千里，烽燧相接也；

translations.literal: Today more than fifty prefectures lie beyond the reach of law and decree. The western Rong are in internal strife, yet recently Jing and Long serve as the frontier—scarcely a thousand li from the capital, with beacon fires linking one to the next;
translations.idiomatic: Today more than fifty prefectures lie beyond the reach of law and decree. The western Rong are in internal strife, yet recently Jing and Long serve as the frontier—scarcely a thousand li from the capital, with beacon fires linking one to the next;

sentences.zh: 加比水旱無年，倉廩空虛。

translations.literal: moreover in recent years flood and drought alternate without respite, and granaries stand empty.
translations.idiomatic: moreover in recent years flood and drought alternate without respite, and granaries stand empty.

sentences.zh: 誠陛下焦心銷誌求濟時之略，渠便高枕而臥哉！」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly burned heart and consumed spirit seeking policies to succor the age, how could you simply rest easy on a high pillow!"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly burned heart and consumed spirit seeking policies to succor the age, how could you simply rest easy on a high pillow!"

sentences.zh: 帝入謂左右曰：「絳言骨鯁，真宰相也。」

translations.literal: The emperor went inside and said to those beside him: "Jiang's words are bone-hard—he is a true chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went inside and said to those beside him, "Jiang's words are bone-hard—he is a true chief minister."

sentences.zh: 遣使者賜酴醿酒。

translations.literal: He sent an envoy to bestow wine of tutilage.
translations.idiomatic: He sent an envoy to bestow wine of tutilage.

sentences.zh: 魏博田季安死，子懷諫弱，軍中請襲節度，吉甫議討之，絳曰：「不然，兩河所懼者，部將以兵圖己也，故委諸將總兵，皆使力敵任均，以相維制，不得為變。

translations.literal: When Tian Ji'an of Weibo died, his son Huaijian was weak. The army asked to inherit the command. Jifu argued for a punitive campaign. Jiang said: "Not so. What the two He regions fear is that their officers will use troops to plot against them. Therefore they entrust the generals with overall command, all made equal in strength and equal in burden, mutually restraining one another so none can rebel.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Ji'an of Weibo died, his son Huaijian was weak. The army asked to inherit the command. Jifu argued for a punitive campaign. Jiang said, "Not so. What the two He regions fear is that their officers will use troops to plot against them. Therefore they entrust the generals with overall command, all made equal in strength and equal in burden, mutually restraining one another so none can rebel.

sentences.zh: 若主帥強，則足以制其命。

translations.literal: If the commander is strong, he can fully control their conduct.
translations.idiomatic: If the commander is strong, he can fully control their conduct.

sentences.zh: 今懷諫乳方臭，不能事，必假權於人，權重則怨生，向之權力均者，將起事生患矣。

translations.literal: Now Huaijian still reeks of milk and cannot govern; he must borrow authority from others. When authority grows heavy, resentment arises; those who once kept power equal will stir up trouble and breed disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Now Huaijian still reeks of milk and cannot govern; he must borrow authority from others. When authority grows heavy, resentment arises; those who once kept power equal will stir up trouble and breed disorder.

sentences.zh: 眾所歸必在寬厚簡易、軍中素所愛者，彼得立，不倚朝廷亦不能安。

translations.literal: Whom the masses follow must be one of generous simplicity whom the army has long loved. When he is established, even without leaning on the court he cannot be secure.
translations.idiomatic: Whom the masses follow must be one of generous simplicity whom the army has long loved. When he is established, even without leaning on the court he cannot be secure.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下蓄威以俟之。」

translations.literal: Only let Your Majesty store up authority and wait."
translations.idiomatic: Only let Your Majesty store up authority and wait."

sentences.zh: 俄而田興果立，以魏博聽命，帝大悅。

translations.literal: Before long Tian Xing was indeed established; Weibo obeyed the court's orders, and the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Tian Xing was indeed established; Weibo obeyed the court's orders, and the emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 吉甫復請命中人宣尉，因刺其變，徐議所宜。

translations.literal: Jifu again asked that a palace envoy be sent to announce consolation, probe their intentions, and slowly discuss what was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu again asked that a palace envoy be sent to announce consolation, probe their intentions, and slowly discuss what was fitting.

sentences.zh: 絳獨謂：「不如推誠撫納，即假旄節。

translations.literal: Jiang alone said: "Better to meet them with sincere trust and conciliation and promptly grant the standard and tokens of command.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang alone said, "Better to meet them with sincere trust and conciliation and promptly grant the standard and tokens of command.

sentences.zh: 它日使者持三軍表來，請與興，則制在彼，不在此，可奏與特授，安得同哉？」

translations.literal: Another day, when an envoy comes bearing the three armies' petition requesting it for Xing, then control lies with them, not with us—we may then memorialize and grant it by special appointment. How can the two cases be the same?"
translations.idiomatic: Another day, when an envoy comes bearing the three armies' petition requesting it for Xing, then control lies with them, not with us—we may then memorialize and grant it by special appointment. How can the two cases be the same?"

sentences.zh: 然帝重違吉甫，故詔張忠順持節往，而授興留後。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor was reluctant to go against Jifu, so he edicted Zhang Zhongshun to go bearing credentials and granted Xing the post of acting commander.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor was reluctant to go against Jifu, so he edicted Zhang Zhongshun to go bearing credentials and granted Xing the post of acting commander.

sentences.zh: 絳固請曰：「如興萬有一不受命，即姑息，復如向時矣。」

translations.literal: Jiang firmly asked: "If by any chance Xing should not accept the order, then it is mere indulgence—the same as before."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang firmly asked, "If by any chance Xing should not accept the order, then it is mere indulgence—the same as before."

sentences.zh: 由是即拜興節度使。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xing was immediately appointed military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Xing was immediately appointed military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 絳復曰：「王化不及魏博久矣，一日挈六州來歸，不大犒賞，人心不激。

translations.literal: Jiang again said: "Imperial transformation has not reached Weibo for a long time. In a single day it brings six prefectures back in submission—without a large reward the people's hearts will not be stirred.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang again said, "Imperial transformation has not reached Weibo for a long time. In a single day it brings six prefectures back in submission—without a large reward the people's hearts will not be stirred.

sentences.zh: 請斥禁錢百五十萬緡賜其軍。」

translations.literal: I ask that one million five hundred thousand strings of cash from the forbidden treasury be released to reward the army."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that one million five hundred thousand strings of cash from the forbidden treasury be released to reward the army."

sentences.zh: 有言太過者，絳曰：「假令舉十五萬眾，期歲而得六州，計所轉給三倍於費。

translations.literal: When some said this was excessive, Jiang said: "Suppose one raised a hundred fifty thousand men and in the space of a year took six prefectures—the cost of provisioning would be triple this sum.
translations.idiomatic: When some said this was excessive, Jiang said, "Suppose one raised a hundred fifty thousand men and in the space of a year took six prefectures—the cost of provisioning would be triple this sum.

sentences.zh: 今興天挺忠義，首變汙俗，破兩河之膽，可嗇小費隳機事哉？」

translations.literal: Now Xing was born upright and loyal, the first to change a corrupt custom and break the courage of the two He regions—can we stint a small expense and ruin the opportunity?"
translations.idiomatic: Now Xing was born upright and loyal, the first to change a corrupt custom and break the courage of the two He regions—can we stint a small expense and ruin the opportunity?"

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 帝患朋黨，以問絳。

translations.literal: The emperor was troubled by factional cliques and asked Jiang about it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was troubled by factional cliques and asked Jiang about it.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「自古人君最惡者朋黨，小人揣知，故常藉口以激怒上心。

translations.literal: He replied: "From antiquity what rulers most hated were factions. Petty men infer this and constantly use it as a pretext to inflame the sovereign's heart.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "From antiquity what rulers most hated were factions. Petty men infer this and constantly use it as a pretext to inflame the sovereign's heart.

sentences.zh: 朋黨者，尋之則無跡，言之則可疑。

translations.literal: Faction: search for it and there is no trace; speak of it and suspicion arises.
translations.idiomatic: Faction: search for it and there is no trace; speak of it and suspicion arises.

sentences.zh: 小人常以利動，不顧忠義；

translations.literal: Petty men are often moved by profit and heed neither loyalty nor righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: Petty men are often moved by profit and heed neither loyalty nor righteousness;

sentences.zh: 君子者，遇主知則進，疑則退，安其位不為它計，故常為奸人所乘。

translations.literal: gentlemen advance when the ruler shows understanding and withdraw when he shows doubt; they keep their positions and do not scheme otherwise—thus they are often taken advantage of by schemers.
translations.idiomatic: gentlemen advance when the ruler shows understanding and withdraw when he shows doubt; they keep their positions and do not scheme otherwise—thus they are often taken advantage of by schemers.

sentences.zh: 夫聖人同跡，賢者求類，是同道也，非黨也。

translations.literal: Sages follow the same tracks; the worthy seek their kind—this is shared Way, not faction.
translations.idiomatic: Sages follow the same tracks; the worthy seek their kind—this is shared Way, not faction.

sentences.zh: 陛下奉遵堯、舜、禹、湯之德，豈謂上與數千年君為黨耶？

translations.literal: Your Majesty reverently follows the virtue of Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang—would one say Your Majesty forms a faction with rulers thousands of years ago?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty reverently follows the virtue of Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang—would one say Your Majesty forms a faction with rulers thousands of years ago?

sentences.zh: 道德同耳。

translations.literal: It is merely that the Way and virtue are the same.
translations.idiomatic: It is merely that the Way and virtue are the same.

sentences.zh: 漢時名節骨鯁士，同心愛國，而宦官小人疾之，起黨錮之獄，訖亡天下。

translations.literal: In Han times, men of repute and bone-hard integrity loved the state with one heart, while eunuchs and petty men hated them and raised the Faction Imprisonment cases, until the realm was lost.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times, men of repute and bone-hard integrity loved the state with one heart, while eunuchs and petty men hated them and raised the Faction Imprisonment cases, until the realm was lost.

sentences.zh: 趨利之人，常為朋比，同其私也；

translations.literal: Those who rush for profit constantly form cliques—joining together in private interest;
translations.idiomatic: Those who rush for profit constantly form cliques—joining together in private interest;

sentences.zh: 守正之人，常遭構毀，違其私也。

translations.literal: those who uphold rectitude constantly suffer fabricated slander—because they oppose private interest.
translations.idiomatic: those who uphold rectitude constantly suffer fabricated slander—because they oppose private interest.

sentences.zh: 小人多，譖言常勝；

translations.literal: Petty men are many; calumny often wins;
translations.idiomatic: Petty men are many; calumny often wins;

sentences.zh: 正人少，直道常不勝。

translations.literal: upright men are few; the straight Way often does not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: upright men are few, and the straight path seldom wins.

sentences.zh: 可不戒哉！」

translations.literal: How could one not be on guard!"
translations.idiomatic: Should one not take warning!"

sentences.zh: 絳居中介特，尤為左右所不悅，遂因以自明。

translations.literal: Jiang held an independent position between them and was especially displeasing to those at the emperor's side; he therefore used this occasion to make himself clear.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang held an independent position between the factions and was especially displeasing to those at the emperor's side; he therefore used this occasion to clarify his own stance.

sentences.zh: 王播為鹽鐵使，而事月進。

translations.literal: Wang Bo served as Salt and Iron Commissioner and made monthly presents to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bo served as Salt and Iron Commissioner and made monthly presents to the court.

sentences.zh: 絳曰：「比禁天下正賦外不得有它獻，而播妄名羨余，不出祿稟家貲，願悉付有司。」

translations.literal: Jiang said: "Recently it was forbidden throughout the realm to make any tribute beyond regular taxes, yet Bo presumptuously labels his gifts surplus revenue, not drawn from salary or household assets—I ask that all of it be handed over to the proper offices."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang said, "Recently it was forbidden throughout the realm to make any tribute beyond regular taxes, yet Bo presumptuously labels his gifts surplus revenue, not drawn from salary or household assets. I ask that all of it be handed over to the proper offices."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Well said."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 訖絳在位，獻不入禁中。

translations.literal: Throughout Jiang's tenure in office, such presents did not enter the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout Jiang's tenure in office, such presents did not enter the palace.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃犯涇州，掠人畜，絳因言：「濱塞虛籍多，實兵少。

translations.literal: The Tibetans invaded Jing prefecture and carried off people and livestock. Jiang therefore said: "Along the border garrisons the rolls are inflated, but actual troops are few.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans invaded Jing prefecture and carried off people and livestock. Jiang therefore said, "Along the border garrisons the rolls are inflated, but actual troops are few.

sentences.zh: 今京西、北神策鎮軍，本防盛秋，坐仰衣食，不使戰。

translations.literal: Now the Shence garrison armies west and north of the capital were originally posted against autumn raids, yet they sit idle receiving food and clothing and are not sent to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Shence garrison armies west and north of the capital were originally posted against autumn raids, yet they sit idle receiving food and clothing and are not sent to fight.

sentences.zh: 事至之日，乃先稟中尉。

translations.literal: When an emergency arises, orders must first be reported to the army supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: When an emergency arises, orders must first be reported to the army supervisors.

sentences.zh: 夫兵不內禦，要須應變，失毫氂，差千里。

translations.literal: Troops ought not be used for internal defense alone; they must be able to respond to changing conditions—miss by a hair's breadth and the error is a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Troops ought not be used for internal defense alone; they must be able to respond to changing conditions. Miss by a hair's breadth and the error is a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 請分隸本道，則號令齊一，前戰不還踵矣。」

translations.literal: I ask that they be assigned to their original circuits; then commands will be unified, and troops in the front need not turn back."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that they be assigned to their original circuits. Then commands will be unified, and troops at the front need not turn back."

sentences.zh: 然士卒樂兩軍姑息，宦者以為言，議遂寢。

translations.literal: However the soldiers were content with the indulgence of the two armies; eunuchs spoke against it, and the proposal was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: However the soldiers were content with the indulgence of the two armies. Eunuchs spoke against it, and the proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 嘗盛夏對延英，帝汗浹衣，絳欲趨出，帝曰：「朕宮中所對，惟宦官、女子，欲與卿講天下事，乃其樂也。」

translations.literal: Once in midsummer at an audience in the Yanying Hall, the emperor's sweat soaked his robes. Jiang wished to withdraw hastily. The emperor said: "In the palace I converse only with eunuchs and women. To discuss the affairs of the realm with you—that is my pleasure."
translations.idiomatic: Once in midsummer at an audience in the Yanying Hall, the emperor's sweat soaked his robes. Jiang wished to withdraw hastily. The emperor said, "In the palace I converse only with eunuchs and women. To discuss the affairs of the realm with you—that is my pleasure."

sentences.zh: 絳或無所論諍，帝輒詰所以然。

translations.literal: When Jiang sometimes offered no remonstrance, the emperor would immediately ask why.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang sometimes offered no remonstrance, the emperor would immediately ask why.

sentences.zh: 又言：「公等得無有姻故冗食者，當為惜官。」

translations.literal: He also said: "You gentlemen surely have no relations or old associates holding idle posts? You ought to be sparing with office."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "You gentlemen surely have no relations or old associates holding idle posts? You ought to be sparing with office."

sentences.zh: 吉甫、權德輿皆稱無有。

translations.literal: Jifu and Quan Deyu both said there were none.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu and Quan Deyu both said there were none.

sentences.zh: 絳曰：「崔祐甫為宰相，不半歲除吏八百人。

translations.literal: Jiang said: "When Cui Youfu served as chief minister, in less than half a year he appointed eight hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang said, "When Cui Youfu served as chief minister, in less than half a year he appointed eight hundred officials.

sentences.zh: 德宗曰：『多公姻故，何耶？』

translations.literal: Dezong said: 'Many are your relations and old associates—why?'
translations.idiomatic: Dezong said, 'Many are your relations and old associates—why?'

sentences.zh: 祐甫曰：『所問當與不當耳，非臣親舊，孰知其才？

translations.literal: Youfu said: 'What matters is whether the appointment is right or wrong. If they were not my kin or old associates, who would know their talent?
translations.idiomatic: Youfu said, 'What matters is whether the appointment is right or wrong. If they were not my kin or old associates, who would know their talent?

sentences.zh: 其不知者，安敢與官？』

translations.literal: Those of whose talent I am ignorant—how would I dare give them office?
translations.idiomatic: Those of whose talent I am ignorant—how would I dare give them office?

sentences.zh: 時以為名言。

translations.literal: At the time this was regarded as a celebrated saying.
translations.idiomatic: At the time this was regarded as a celebrated saying.

sentences.zh: 武後命官猥多，而開元中有名者皆出其選。

translations.literal: Empress Wu's appointments were excessively numerous, yet the celebrated men of the Kaiyuan era all came from her selections.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu's appointments were excessively numerous, yet the celebrated men of the Kaiyuan era all came from her selections.

sentences.zh: 古人言拔十得五，猶得其半。

translations.literal: The ancients said that if you choose ten and get five, you still have half.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said that if you choose ten and get five, you still have half.

sentences.zh: 若情故自嫌，非聖主責成意。」

translations.literal: If one shrinks from personal ties, that is not what a sage ruler intends when he charges you with results."
translations.idiomatic: If one shrinks from personal ties, that is not what a sage ruler intends when he charges you with results."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「誠然，在至當而已。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Indeed—it is merely a matter of what is perfectly fitting."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Indeed—it is merely a matter of what is perfectly fitting."

sentences.zh: 帝又問：「玄宗開元時致治，天寶則亂，何一君而相反耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor also asked: "Under Xuanzong the Kaiyuan era brought good governance, but the Tianbao era brought disorder—how could one ruler be so opposite to himself?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also asked, "Under Xuanzong the Kaiyuan era brought good governance, but the Tianbao era brought disorder—how could one ruler be so opposite to himself?"

sentences.zh: 絳曰：「治生於憂危，亂生於放肆。

translations.literal: Jiang said: "Order arises from worry and peril; disorder arises from license.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang said, "Order arises from worry and peril; disorder arises from license.

sentences.zh: 玄宗嘗歷試官守，知人之艱難，臨禦初，任用姚崇、宋璟，勵精聽納，故左右前後皆正人也。

translations.literal: Xuanzong had once served in trial posts as prefect and minister and knew the difficulty of assessing men. At the start of his reign he employed Yao Chong and Song Jing, exerting himself in diligence and heeding counsel—thus those at his side and all around were upright men.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong had once served in trial posts as prefect and minister and knew the difficulty of assessing men. At the start of his reign he employed Yao Chong and Song Jing, exerting himself in diligence and heeding counsel, so those at his side and all around were upright men.

sentences.zh: 洎林甫、國忠得君，專引傾邪之人，分總要劇。

translations.literal: When Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong gained the ruler's trust, they exclusively brought in corrupt men and divided among themselves the weightiest duties.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong gained the ruler's trust, they exclusively brought in corrupt men and divided among themselves the weightiest duties.

sentences.zh: 於是上不聞直言，嗜欲日滋，內則盜臣勸以興利，外則武夫誘以開邊，天下騷動，故祿山乘隙而奮。

translations.literal: Thereupon the ruler above no longer heard plain speech; appetites daily increased; within, grasping ministers urged profit-making; without, warriors enticed frontier campaigns—the realm seethed, and so An Lushan seized the opening and rose up.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the ruler above no longer heard plain speech; appetites daily increased. Within, grasping ministers urged profit-making; without, warriors enticed frontier campaigns. The realm seethed, and so An Lushan seized the opening and rose up.

sentences.zh: 此皆小人啟導，從逸而驕。

translations.literal: All this was the leading of petty men—from ease to arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: All this was the leading of petty men—from ease to arrogance.

sentences.zh: 系時主所行，無常治，亦無常亂。」

translations.literal: It depended on what the ruler of the time did—there is no constant order, and no constant disorder."
translations.idiomatic: It depended on what the ruler of the time did—there is no constant order, and no constant disorder."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「凡人舉事，病不通於理，追咎其失，古人處此有道耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When anyone undertakes a task, the fault is not understanding principle; when one revisits one's mistakes afterward, did the ancients have a Way for this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When anyone undertakes a task, the fault is not understanding principle. When one revisits one's mistakes afterward, did the ancients have a Way for this?"

sentences.zh: 絳曰：「事或過差，聖哲所不免。

translations.literal: Jiang said: "Matters may overshoot—even sages cannot avoid this.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang said, "Matters may overshoot—even sages cannot avoid this.

sentences.zh: 天子有諫臣，所以救過。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven has remonstrance ministers—that is how errors are remedied.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven has remonstrance ministers—that is how errors are remedied.

sentences.zh: 上下同體，猶手足之於心膂，交相為用。

translations.literal: Ruler and minister share one body, like hands and feet to the heart and backbone—each serving the other.
translations.idiomatic: Ruler and minister share one body, like hands and feet to the heart and backbone—each serving the other.

sentences.zh: 但矜能護失，常情所蔽，聖人改過不吝，願陛下以此處之。」

translations.literal: Yet pride in one's ability and shielding one's faults are common blindness. Sages do not grudge correcting error—I pray Your Majesty handle matters in this spirit."
translations.idiomatic: Yet pride in one's ability and shielding one's faults are common blindness. Sages do not grudge correcting error. I pray Your Majesty handle matters in this spirit."

sentences.zh: 教坊使稱密詔閱良家子及別宅婦人內禁中，京師囂然。

translations.literal: The Director of the Music Bureau claimed a secret edict to inspect sons of good families and women from separate residences for admission to the inner palace—the capital was in an uproar.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Music Bureau claimed a secret edict to inspect sons of good families and women from separate residences for admission to the inner palace, and the capital was in an uproar.

sentences.zh: 絳將入言於帝，吉甫曰：「此諫官所論列。」

translations.literal: Jiang was about to enter and speak to the emperor. Jifu said: "This is something for remonstrance officials to discuss."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang was about to enter and speak to the emperor. Jifu said, "This is something for remonstrance officials to discuss."

sentences.zh: 絳曰：「公嘗病諫官論事，此難言者，欲移之耶？」

translations.literal: Jiang said: "You once complained that remonstrance officials raised too many matters. This is a hard thing to speak of—do you wish to shift it onto them?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiang said, "You once complained that remonstrance officials raised too many matters. This is a hard thing to speak of—do you wish to shift it onto them?"

sentences.zh: 吉甫乃欲諷詔使止之，絳以吉甫畏不敢諫，遂獨上疏。

translations.literal: Jifu then wanted to prompt an edict to stop it. Jiang, taking Jifu to be afraid and not daring to remonstrate, submitted a memorial alone.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu then wanted to prompt an edict to stop it. Jiang, taking Jifu to be afraid and not daring to remonstrate, submitted a memorial alone.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕以丹王等無侍者，比命訪閭裏，以貲致之，彼不諭朕意，故至嘩擾。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Because the Prince of Dan and others had no attendants, I recently ordered inquiries in the lanes to obtain them by payment—they did not understand my intent, and thus the commotion arose."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Because the Prince of Dan and others had no attendants, I recently ordered inquiries in the lanes to obtain them by payment. They did not understand my intent, and thus the commotion arose."

sentences.zh: 乃悉歸所取。

translations.literal: All those taken were then returned.
translations.idiomatic: All those taken were then returned.

sentences.zh: 以足疾求免，罷為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness of the feet and asked to be relieved; he was dismissed from his chief ministership and made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness of the feet and asked to be relieved. He was dismissed from his chief ministership and made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 帝乃召承璀於淮南。

translations.literal: The emperor then summoned Cheng Cui from Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then summoned Cheng Cui from Huainan.

sentences.zh: 絳雖去位，猶懷不能已，因上言：「北虜方強，其憂有五。

translations.literal: Though Jiang had left office, his concern could not cease; he submitted a memorial: "The northern barbarians are strong just now; there are five worries.
translations.idiomatic: Though Jiang had left office, his concern could not cease. He submitted a memorial: "The northern barbarians are strong just now; there are five worries.

sentences.zh: 彼蔑信重利，歲入馬求直，今則置不取，當貯他謀，一也。

translations.literal: They hold treaties in contempt and value profit highly. Each year they entered horses seeking payment; now we refuse to take them—they must be storing up some other design. That is the first.
translations.idiomatic: They hold treaties in contempt and value profit highly. Each year they entered horses seeking payment; now we refuse to take them—they must be storing up some other design. That is the first.

sentences.zh: 屯士不足，斥候不明，城無完堞，非可應卒，二也。

translations.literal: Garrison troops are insufficient, scouts are unclear, and city walls lack intact parapets—this cannot meet sudden emergencies. That is the second.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison troops are insufficient, scouts are unclear, and city walls lack intact parapets—this cannot meet sudden emergencies. That is the second.

sentences.zh: 今之營築，不詢眾謀，遠規塞外，城非要地，虜一入寇，應援艱阻，三也。

translations.literal: Present fortification work consults no broad counsel; it looks far beyond the passes and builds where the ground is not vital. If the barbarians raid once, relief will be hard pressed to arrive. That is the third.
translations.idiomatic: Present fortification work consults no broad counsel. It looks far beyond the passes and builds where the ground is not vital. If the barbarians raid once, relief will be hard pressed to arrive. That is the third.

sentences.zh: 比年通好，往來窺覘，河山兵甲，悉知之矣，若寇掠驅脅，援兵非十日不至，既至虜去，兵罷復來，四也。

translations.literal: In recent years of friendly relations, they came and went spying—the rivers, mountains, and armaments are all known to them. If they raid and drive people off, relief cannot arrive in less than ten days; once it arrives the barbarians are gone, and when the troops stand down they come again. That is the fourth.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years of friendly relations, they came and went spying—the rivers, mountains, and armaments are all known to them. If they raid and drive people off, relief cannot arrive in less than ten days. Once it arrives the barbarians are gone, and when the troops stand down they come again. That is the fourth.

sentences.zh: 北狄、西戎久為仇敵，今回鶻思叛，脫相連約，數道並進，何以遏之？

translations.literal: The northern Di and the western Rong have long been mutual enemies. Now the Uyghurs consider rebellion; if by chance they join in treaty and advance on several routes together, how could we check them?
translations.idiomatic: The northern Di and the western Rong have long been mutual enemies. Now the Uyghurs consider rebellion. If by chance they join in treaty and advance on several routes together, how could we check them?

sentences.zh: 五也。」

translations.literal: That is the fifth."
translations.idiomatic: That is the fifth."

sentences.zh: 十年，出為華州刺史。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he went out to serve as prefect of Hua.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he went out to serve as prefect of Hua.

sentences.zh: 承璀田多在部中，主奴擾民，絳捕系之。

translations.literal: Cheng Cui's fields were mostly in that prefecture; his stewards and slaves harassed the people. Jiang had them arrested and bound.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Cui's fields were mostly in that prefecture. His stewards and slaves harassed the people, and Jiang had them arrested and bound.

sentences.zh: 會遣五坊使，帝戒曰：「至華宜自戢；

translations.literal: When the Five-Workshop envoys were sent out, the emperor warned them: "When you reach Hua you ought to restrain yourselves;
translations.idiomatic: When the Five-Workshop envoys were sent out, the emperor warned them, "When you reach Hua you ought to restrain yourselves;

sentences.zh: 絳，大臣，有奏即行法矣。」

translations.literal: Jiang is a great minister—if he memorializes about you, the law will be applied at once."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang is a great minister—if he memorializes about you, the law will be applied at once."

sentences.zh: 州有捕鷂戶，歲責貢限，絳以為言，並勸止畋獵，有詔澤潞、太原、天威府並罷之。

translations.literal: The prefecture had households that captured hawks, with annual tribute quotas. Jiang spoke against this and also urged an end to hunting. An edict abolished these offices in Ze, Lu, Taiyuan, and Tianwei prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had households that captured hawks, with annual tribute quotas. Jiang spoke against this and also urged an end to hunting. An edict abolished these offices in Ze, Lu, Taiyuan, and Tianwei prefecture.

sentences.zh: 入為兵部尚書，母喪免。

translations.literal: He returned to court as Minister of War, then resigned on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as Minister of War, then resigned on his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 還授河中觀察使。

translations.literal: On returning from mourning he was appointed observation commissioner of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from mourning he was appointed observation commissioner of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 河中故節制，而皇甫镈惡絳，故薄其恩，議者不直。

translations.literal: Hezhong had formerly been a military commission; Huangfu Bo hated Jiang and therefore stinted his favor—the commentators did not regard this as fair.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong had formerly been a military commission. Huangfu Bo hated Jiang and therefore stinted his favor, and commentators did not regard this as fair.

sentences.zh: 镈得罪，復以兵部召。

translations.literal: When Bo fell from favor, Jiang was again summoned as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Bo fell from favor, Jiang was again summoned as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 遷御史大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 穆宗數遊畋，絳率其屬叩延英切諫，不納。

translations.literal: Muzong frequently went hunting. Jiang led his subordinates to knock at the Yanying gate and remonstrate urgently—they were not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong frequently went hunting. Jiang led his subordinates to knock at the Yanying gate and remonstrate urgently, but they were not heeded.

sentences.zh: 以疾辭，還兵部尚書，歷東都留守，徙東川節度使，復為留守。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and resigned, returning as Minister of War; he served successively as Eastern Capital left-behind commissioner, was transferred to military commissioner of Dongchuan, and again served as left-behind commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and resigned, returning as Minister of War. He served successively as Eastern Capital left-behind commissioner, was transferred to military commissioner of Dongchuan, and again served as left-behind commissioner.

sentences.zh: 寶歷初，拜尚書左仆射。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Baoli era he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Baoli era he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 絳偉儀質，以直道進退，望冠一時，賢不肖太分，屢為讒邪所中。

translations.literal: Jiang was imposing in bearing and steadfast in advancing and withdrawing by the straight Way; his renown topped his age. He divided the worthy and unworthy too sharply and was repeatedly struck by slanderous wicked men.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang was imposing in bearing and steadfast in advancing and withdrawing by the straight Way; his renown topped his age. He divided the worthy and unworthy too sharply and was repeatedly struck down by slanderous wicked men.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞王璠遇絳於道，不之避。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Fan met Jiang on the road and did not yield to him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Fan met Jiang on the road and did not yield to him.

sentences.zh: 絳引故事論列，宰相李逢吉右璠，下遷絳太子少師，分司東都。

translations.literal: Jiang cited precedent and memorialized. Chief Minister Li Fengji sided with Fan; Jiang was demoted to Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent with assignment at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang cited precedent and memorialized. Chief Minister Li Fengji sided with Fan, and Jiang was demoted to Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent with assignment at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 文宗立，召為太常卿，以檢校司空為山南西道節度使，累封趙郡公。

translations.literal: When Wenzong ascended, Jiang was summoned as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; as Acting Minister of Works he became military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit, and was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong ascended, Jiang was summoned as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. As Acting Minister of Works he became military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit and was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 四年，南蠻寇蜀道，詔絳募兵千人往赴，不半道，蠻已去，兵還。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, southern barbarians raided the Shu road. An edict ordered Jiang to raise a thousand troops to go to the rescue. Before they were halfway there the barbarians had already gone, and the troops returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, southern barbarians raided the Shu road. An edict ordered Jiang to raise a thousand troops to go to the rescue. Before they were halfway there the barbarians had already gone, and the troops returned.

sentences.zh: 監軍使楊叔元者，素疾絳，遣人迎說軍曰：「將收募直而還為民。」

translations.literal: The army supervisor Yang Shuyuan had long resented Jiang. He sent men to meet the troops and told them: "The commander intends to take the enlistment pay and send you back to be civilians."
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisor Yang Shuyuan had long resented Jiang. He sent men to meet the troops and told them, "The commander intends to take the enlistment pay and send you back to be civilians."

sentences.zh: 士皆怒，乃噪而入，劫庫兵。

translations.literal: The soldiers were all enraged; they raised a clamor and burst in, seizing weapons from the arsenal.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers were all enraged. They raised a clamor and burst in, seizing weapons from the arsenal.

sentences.zh: 絳方宴，不設備，遂握節登陴。

translations.literal: Jiang was at a banquet and made no preparations; he then grasped his credential and mounted the ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang was at a banquet and made no preparations. He then grasped his credential and mounted the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 或言縋城可以免，絳不從。

translations.literal: Some said he could escape by lowering himself from the wall by rope—Jiang would not.
translations.idiomatic: Some said he could escape by lowering himself from the wall by rope, but Jiang would not.

sentences.zh: 牙將王景延力戰歿，絳遂遇害，年六十七。

translations.literal: Defensive officer Wang Jingyan fought fiercely and died; Jiang was then killed at age sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Defensive officer Wang Jingyan fought fiercely and died. Jiang was then killed at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 幕府趙存約、薛齊皆死。

translations.literal: Staff members Zhao Cunyue and Xue Qi both died.
translations.idiomatic: Staff members Zhao Cunyue and Xue Qi both died.

sentences.zh: 事聞，諫官崔戎等列絳冤，冊贈司徒，謚曰貞，賻禮甚厚。

translations.literal: When word reached court, remonstrance officials such as Cui Rong set forth Jiang's grievance. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor with posthumous title Zhen, and funeral gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached court, remonstrance officials such as Cui Rong set forth Jiang's grievance. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor with the posthumous title Zhen, and funeral gifts were very generous.

sentences.zh: 景延亦贈官，祿一子。

translations.literal: Jingyan was also granted posthumous office and one son was given salary.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyan was also granted posthumous office, and one son was given a salary.

sentences.zh: 大中初，詔史官差第元和將相，圖形淩煙閣，絳在焉，獨留中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dazhong era, an edict ordered the historiographers to rank the chief ministers and generals of the Yuanhe era and portray them in the Lingyan Pavilion. Jiang was among them, kept only within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Dazhong era, an edict ordered the historiographers to rank the chief ministers and generals of the Yuanhe era and portray them in the Lingyan Pavilion. Jiang was among them, with his portrait kept only within the palace.

sentences.zh: 絳所論事萬餘言，其甥夏侯孜以授蔣偕，次為七篇。

translations.literal: Jiang's memorials on affairs ran to more than ten thousand words. His nephew Xiahou Zi gave them to Jiang Xie, who arranged them into seven sections.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang's memorials on affairs ran to more than ten thousand words. His nephew Xiahou Zi gave them to Jiang Xie, who arranged them into seven sections.

sentences.zh: 子璋，字重禮。

translations.literal: His son Zhang, style name Chongli.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhang, courtesy name Chongli.

sentences.zh: 大中初擢進士第，辟盧鈞太原幕府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong he passed the jinshi examination and was invited to Lu Jun's Taiyuan headquarters staff.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Dazhong he passed the jinshi examination and was invited to Lu Jun's Taiyuan headquarters staff.

sentences.zh: 遷監察御史，奏太廟祫享復用宰相攝事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant Censor and memorialized that at the Great Temple joint autumnal sacrifices the chief ministers should again act in proxy.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Palace Attendant Censor and memorialized that at the Great Temple joint autumnal sacrifices the chief ministers should again act in proxy.

sentences.zh: 進起居郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Diarist.

sentences.zh: 舊制，設次郊丘，太仆盤車載樂，召群臣臨觀，璋奏罷之。

translations.literal: Under the old system, on staging at the suburban altars the Imperial Stud used a turntable carriage to carry music, and all officials were summoned to witness it. Zhang memorialized to abolish this.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, on staging at the suburban altars the Imperial Stud used a turntable carriage to carry music, and all officials were summoned to witness it. Zhang memorialized to abolish the practice.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，累官尚書右丞、湖南宣歙觀察使。

translations.literal: During the Xiantong era he rose in succession to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and observation commissioner of Hunan, Xuan, and She.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiantong era he rose in succession to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and observation commissioner of Hunan, Xuan, and She.

sentences.zh: 宋申錫，字慶臣，史失其何所人。

translations.literal: Song Shenxi, style name Qingchen—the history loses which place he was from.
translations.idiomatic: Song Shenxi, courtesy name Qingchen—the history does not record his native place.

sentences.zh: 少而孤，擢進士第，累辟節度府，後頻遷起居舍人，以禮部員外郎為翰林學士。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, he passed the jinshi examination, was repeatedly invited to military headquarters staffs, later rose in succession to Diarist, and served as Hanlin Academician while Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly invited to military headquarters staffs. He later rose in succession to Diarist and served as Hanlin Academician while Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 敬宗時，拜侍講學士。

translations.literal: During Jingzong's reign he was appointed Lecturing Academician.
translations.idiomatic: During Jingzong's reign he was appointed Lecturing Academician.

sentences.zh: 長慶、寶歷間，風俗囂薄，驅煽朋黨，申錫素孤直少與，及進用，議者謂可以激浮競。

translations.literal: During the Changqing and Baoli eras, customs were clamorous and shallow; cliques drove and inflamed one another. Shenxi had always been upright and isolated with few associates; when he was promoted, commentators said he could stir against empty rivalry.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changqing and Baoli eras, customs were clamorous and shallow, and cliques drove and inflamed one another. Shenxi had always been upright and isolated with few associates. When he was promoted, commentators said he could stir against empty rivalry.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，再轉中書舍人，復為翰林學士。

translations.literal: When Wenzong ascended, he was twice transferred to Drafting Secretariat Drafter and again served as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong ascended, he was twice transferred to Drafting Secretariat Drafter and again served as Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 帝惡宦官權寵震主，再致宮禁之變，而王守澄典禁兵，偃蹇放肆，欲剟除本根，思可與決大議者。

translations.literal: The emperor hated that eunuchs' power and favor shook the throne and twice brought palace upheavals. Wang Shoucheng commanded the forbidden armies, arrogant and unrestrained. The emperor wished to cut out the root and sought someone with whom he could decide great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hated that eunuchs' power and favor shook the throne and twice brought palace upheavals. Wang Shoucheng commanded the forbidden armies, arrogant and unrestrained. The emperor wished to cut out the root and sought someone with whom he could decide great affairs.

sentences.zh: 察申錫忠厚，因召對，俾與朝臣謀去守澄等，且倚以執政，申錫頓首謝。

translations.literal: Finding Shenxi honest and steadfast, he summoned him for audience, had him join court ministers in plotting to remove Shoucheng and the others, and intended to rely on him to govern. Shenxi kowtowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Shenxi honest and steadfast, he summoned him for audience, had him join court ministers in plotting to remove Shoucheng and the others, and intended to rely on him to govern. Shenxi kowtowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 未幾拜尚書右丞，逾月進同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; after a month he was advanced to Co-signer of the Central Secretariat and the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs. After a month he was advanced to Co-signer of the Central Secretariat and the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 乃除王璠京兆尹，密諭帝旨。

translations.literal: He then appointed Wang Fan Intendant of Jingzhao and secretly conveyed the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed Wang Fan Intendant of Jingzhao and secretly conveyed the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 璠漏言，而守澄黨鄭註得其謀。

translations.literal: Fan leaked word of it, and Shoucheng's faction member Zheng Zhu learned of the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Fan leaked word of it, and Shoucheng's faction member Zheng Zhu learned of the plot.

sentences.zh: 太和五年，遣軍候豆盧著誣告申錫與漳王謀反，守澄持奏浴堂，將遣騎二百屠申錫家，宦官馬存亮爭曰：「謀反者獨申錫耳，當召南司會議，不然，京師跂足亂矣。」

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe, he sent Army Aide Dou Luzhuo to lodge a false accusation that Shenxi and the Prince of Zhang plotted rebellion. Shoucheng brought the memorial to the Bath Hall and was about to send two hundred riders to slaughter Shenxi's household. Eunuch Ma Cunliang objected: "The rebel is Shenxi alone. The Court of Southern Affairs should be summoned to deliberate; otherwise the capital will rise on tiptoe in disorder."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taihe, he sent Army Aide Dou Luzhuo to lodge a false accusation that Shenxi and the Prince of Zhang plotted rebellion. Shoucheng brought the memorial to the Bath Hall and was about to send two hundred riders to slaughter Shenxi's household. Eunuch Ma Cunliang objected, "The rebel is Shenxi alone. The Court of Southern Affairs should be summoned to deliberate; otherwise the capital will rise on tiptoe in disorder."

sentences.zh: 守澄不能對。

translations.literal: Shoucheng could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Shoucheng could not reply.

sentences.zh: 時二月晦，群司皆休，中人馳召宰相，馬奔乏死於道，易所乘以復命。

translations.literal: It was the last day of the second month; all offices were closed. Palace eunuchs galloped to summon the chief ministers; horses ran until exhausted and died on the road, and other mounts were taken to deliver the reply.
translations.idiomatic: It was the last day of the second month, and all offices were closed. Palace eunuchs galloped to summon the chief ministers. Horses ran until exhausted and died on the road, and other mounts were taken to deliver the reply.

sentences.zh: 申錫與牛僧孺、路隋、李宗閔至中書，中人唱曰：「所召無宋申錫。」

translations.literal: Shenxi arrived at the Secretariat with Niu Sengru, Lu Sui, and Li Zongmin; a palace attendant announced: "Among those summoned there is no Song Shenxi."
translations.idiomatic: Shenxi arrived at the Secretariat with Niu Sengru, Lu Sui, and Li Zongmin. A palace attendant announced, "Among those summoned there is no Song Shenxi."

sentences.zh: 申錫始知得罪，望延英門，以笏叩額還第。

translations.literal: Shenxi then knew he had offended; he gazed toward the Yan Ying Gate, struck his forehead with his tablet, and returned to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxi then knew he had fallen from favor. He gazed toward Yan Ying Gate, struck his forehead with his court tablet, and returned home.

sentences.zh: 僧孺等見上出著告牒，皆駭愕不知所對。

translations.literal: Sengru and the others saw the emperor produce Zhu's denunciation and were all alarmed and at a loss for a reply.
translations.idiomatic: Sengru and the others saw the emperor produce Zhu's denunciation. They were all stunned and did not know what to say.

sentences.zh: 守澄捕申錫親吏張全真、家人買子緣信及十六宅典史，脅成其罪。

translations.literal: Shoucheng arrested Shenxi's close clerk Zhang Quanzhen, household member Maizi Yuanxin, and clerks of the Sixteen Mansions, and coerced them into completing the charge.
translations.idiomatic: Shoucheng arrested Shenxi's close clerk Zhang Quanzhen, his household retainer Maizi Yuanxin, and clerks of the Sixteen Mansions, and coerced them into fabricating the case.

sentences.zh: 帝乃罷申錫為太子右庶子，召三省官、御史中丞、大理卿、京兆尹會中書集賢院雜驗申錫反狀。

translations.literal: The emperor then removed Shenxi to Right Vice Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and summoned officials of the Three Departments, the Vice Censor-in-Chief, the Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review, and the Jingzhao magistrate to meet at the Secretariat and Hall of Assembled Worthies to examine together the facts of Shenxi's rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then demoted Shenxi to Right Vice Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and summoned officials of the Three Departments, the Vice Censor-in-Chief, the chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review, and the Jingzhao magistrate to meet at the Secretariat and Hall of Assembled Worthies to examine the charges of rebellion against Shenxi.

sentences.zh: 京師嘩言相驚，久乃定。

translations.literal: In the capital there was clamor and mutual alarm; only after a long while did things settle.
translations.idiomatic: The capital erupted in rumor and alarm, and only after a long while did order return.

sentences.zh: 翌日，延英召宰相群官悉入，初議抵申錫死，仆射竇易直率然對曰：「人臣無將，將而必誅。」

translations.literal: The next day, at Yan Ying all the chief ministers and officials were summoned in; at first they debated sentencing Shenxi to death. The Left Vice Director Dou Yizhi answered bluntly: "A minister must not harbor designs of rebellion; if he does, he must be put to death."
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor summoned all the chief ministers and officials to Yan Ying Hall. At first they debated sentencing Shenxi to death. Left Vice Director Dou Yizhi answered bluntly, "A minister must not harbor designs of rebellion; if he does, he must be executed."

sentences.zh: 聞者不然。

translations.literal: Those who heard this did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard this were not persuaded.

sentences.zh: 於是左散騎常侍崔玄亮、給事中李固言、諫議大夫王質、補闕盧鈞、舒元褒、羅泰、蔣系、裴休、竇宗直、韋溫，拾遺李群、韋端符、丁居晦、袁都等伏殿陛，請以獄付外。

translations.literal: Thereupon Left Regular Attendant Cui Xuanliang, Supervising Secretary Li Guyin, Remonstrating Grand Master Wang Zhi, Supplements Lu Jun, Shu Yuanbao, Luo Tai, Jiang Xi, Pei Xiu, Dou Zongzhi, and Wei Wen, and Reminders Li Qun, Wei Duanfu, Ding Juhui, Yuan Du, and others prostrated themselves on the palace steps and asked that the case be handed over to the outer offices.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Cui Xuanliang, Li Guyin, Wang Zhi, Lu Jun, Shu Yuanbao, Luo Tai, Jiang Xi, Pei Xiu, Dou Zongzhi, Wei Wen, Li Qun, Wei Duanfu, Ding Juhui, Yuan Du, and others prostrated themselves on the palace steps and asked that the case be referred to the regular judicial offices.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，叱曰：「吾與公卿議矣，卿屬第出！」

translations.literal: The emperor was shaken with anger and shouted: "I have already deliberated with the chief ministers and officials—you lot, withdraw in order!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and shouted, "I have already deliberated with the chief ministers and officials. You lot, withdraw at once!"

sentences.zh: 玄亮、固言執據愈切，涕泣懇到，繇是議貸申錫於嶺表。

translations.literal: Xuanliang and Guyin pressed their argument all the more urgently, weeping with earnest pleading; because of this the deliberation was to spare Shenxi and banish him to the Lingnan frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanliang and Guyin pressed their argument all the more urgently, weeping with earnest pleading. Because of this the court decided to spare Shenxi's life and banish him to the Lingnan frontier.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹崔琯、大理卿王正雅苦請出著與申錫劾正情狀，帝悟，乃貶申錫開州司馬，從而流死者數十百人，天下以為冤。

translations.literal: Jingzhao magistrate Cui Guan and Chief Judge Wang Zhengya earnestly asked that Zhu be produced and the true circumstances of the accusation against Shenxi be examined; the emperor came to his senses and demoted Shenxi to Defender of Kai prefecture. In the aftermath several tens or hundreds died in exile, and all under Heaven regarded it as a wrongful case.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao magistrate Cui Guan and chief judge Wang Zhengya earnestly asked that Zhu be produced so the true circumstances of the case against Shenxi could be examined. The emperor came to his senses and demoted Shenxi to defender of Kai prefecture. In the aftermath scores died in exile, and the empire regarded it as a grave injustice.

sentences.zh: 擢豆盧著兼殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Doulu Zhu was promoted to Concurrent Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Doulu Zhu was promoted to concurrent Palace Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 初，申錫既歸，易素服俟命外舍，其妻責謂曰：「公何負天子，乃反乎？」

translations.literal: At first, after Shenxi had returned home, Yi wore plain clothes and waited for orders in an outer room. His wife reproached him, saying: "What have you done to wrong the Son of Heaven that you would rebel?"
translations.idiomatic: When Shenxi returned home, he wore plain clothes and waited for orders in an outer room. His wife reproached him, saying, "What have you done to wrong the Son of Heaven that you would be called a rebel?"

sentences.zh: 申錫曰：「吾起孤生，位宰相，蒙國厚恩，不能鉏奸亂，反為所陷，我豈反者乎？」

translations.literal: Shenxi said: "I rose from solitary birth to the rank of chief minister and received the state's thick grace. I could not cut down treachery and disorder and was instead trapped by it—how could I be a rebel?"
translations.idiomatic: Shenxi said, "I rose from humble origins to the chancellorship and received the state's great favor. I could not cut down treachery and disorder and was instead trapped by it. How could I be a rebel?"

sentences.zh: 初，申錫以清節進，疾要位者納賕餉，敗風俗，故自為近臣，凡四方賄謝一不受。

translations.literal: From the first Shenxi had advanced through pure integrity; he detested those in high position who accepted bribes and gifts and corrupted custom. Therefore, once he became a close minister, he accepted none of the bribes and gifts of thanks from the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxi had risen through pure integrity and detested powerful men who accepted bribes and corrupted public morals. Once he became a close minister, he refused every gift and bribe sent from the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 既被罪，有司驗劾，悉得所還問遺書，朝野為咨閔。

translations.literal: After he was charged, the authorities investigated and verified, and recovered all the letters of inquiry and gifts he had returned; court and country sighed in sympathy.
translations.idiomatic: After he was charged, the authorities investigated and recovered all the letters and gifts he had returned unopened. Court and country sighed in sympathy.

sentences.zh: 然在宰府無它謀略。

translations.literal: Yet in the chief minister's office he had no other stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the chancellery he had shown little strategic capacity.

sentences.zh: 七年，感憤卒，有詔歸葬。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died of indignant grief; an edict ordered his burial to be conducted at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he died of grief and indignation. An edict ordered his remains returned for burial.

sentences.zh: 開成元年，李石因延英召對，從容言曰：「陛下之政，皆承天心，惟申錫之枉，久未原雪。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaicheng, Li Shi, summoned to audience at Yan Ying, said at ease: "Your Majesty's government all follows Heaven's heart, yet Shenxi's wrongful case has long gone unredressed."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaicheng, Li Shi was summoned to audience at Yan Ying Hall and said calmly, "Your Majesty's government follows Heaven's intent in all things, yet Shenxi's wrongful case has long gone unredressed."

sentences.zh: 帝慚曰：「我當時亦悟其失，而詐忠者迫我以社稷計故耳。

translations.literal: The emperor said in shame: "I too came to see the error at the time, but those who feigned loyalty pressed me with calculations for the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said in shame, "I too came to see the error at the time, but men who feigned loyalty pressed me with arguments for the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 使逢漢昭、宣時，當不坐此。」

translations.literal: Had he met the times of Han Zhao and Xuan, he would not have suffered this punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Had he lived in the times of the Han emperors Zhao and Xuan, he would not have suffered such a fate."

sentences.zh: 因追復右丞、同中書門下平章事，贈兵部尚書，錄其子慎微為城固尉。

translations.literal: He thereupon posthumously restored him as Right Vice Director and Concurrent Grand Councilor, enfeoffed him as Minister of War, and appointed his son Shenwei as magistrate of Chenggu.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon posthumously restored Shenxi as Right Vice Director and concurrent Grand Councilor, enfeoffed him as Minister of War, and appointed his son Shenwei as magistrate of Chenggu.

sentences.zh: 會昌二年，賜謚曰貞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huichang he was granted the posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huichang he was granted the posthumous title Zhen.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：鎰、元衡暴忠王室，絳巨德大臣，皆為賊奸所乘，不歿元身，蓋福善禍淫之訓有時而橈。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Yi and Yuanheng openly displayed loyalty to the royal house; Jiang was a great minister of towering virtue—all were taken advantage of by villainous traitors and did not die a natural death. Perhaps the teaching that fortune follows the good and calamity the wicked is sometimes bent aside.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Yi and Yuanheng openly displayed loyalty to the throne; Jiang was a great minister of towering virtue. All were undone by villainous traitors and did not die natural deaths. Perhaps the teaching that fortune follows the good and calamity the wicked is sometimes bent aside.

sentences.zh: 雖然，賢者於忠誼，寧以一不幸，遽使慊然於其心哉！

translations.literal: Even so, would the worthy, in loyalty and righteousness, because of one misfortune suddenly let resentment fill their hearts?
translations.idiomatic: Even so, would the worthy, in loyalty and righteousness, let one misfortune suddenly fill their hearts with resentment!

sentences.zh: 要躬可殞，而名與岱、崧等矣。

translations.literal: Their persons might perish, yet their names stand equal to Mount Tai and Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: Their bodies might perish, yet their names stand with Mount Tai and Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 公輔隙開，而猶納說焉。

translations.literal: Though a rift opened with Gongfu, he still accepted his remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Though a rift had opened between them, the emperor still heeded Gongfu's remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 申錫謀小任大，顛沛從之，惜乎！

translations.literal: Shenxi's plans were small for the great charge he bore; he was driven to hardship in their wake—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Shenxi's plans were too slight for the great charge he bore, and hardship followed in their wake. Alas!
